title: I finally got my hands on the Unistellar Envision smart binoculars with augmented reality and I can’t wait to stargaze with them
content:
The Unistellar Envision smart binoculars, announced in 2024, are the first pair of smart binoculars designed specifically for night sky observation. They feature an augmented reality (AR) overlay in the right-hand lens that identifies night sky targets, including planets, stars, and deep space objects, as well as landmarks and navigational tools. The device is pre-ordered for $1,499 or £1,299 and ships with a soft carry case, padded neck strap, USB-C cable, and rubber caps for the eyepieces and lenses.

The binoculars have a solid build, though they are not the most lightweight option due to the embedded technology. They feature 10x magnification and 50mm objective lenses, which provide strong light-gathering power essential for stargazing. The control panel includes five buttons on the top: the left side controls guided tour advancement, target lock selection, and display mode, while the right side houses the calibration and power buttons, with the power button also serving as a switch for the AR display. A central focus wheel allows for manual adjustments, though it requires two hands to operate.

Setting up the device is recommended during the daytime to allow time for familiarization with the controls and diopter adjustment. After powering on, the binoculars connect to the Unistellar app, which recognizes the device and provides onboarding videos. Users are advised to perform a 360-degree calibration before first use and to set location services to "always" to ensure accurate AR readings for target locations.

In daytime testing, the topographical identification feature successfully identified local landmarks, and the target lock feature allowed a friend to easily locate a geographical landmark via the AR indicator. However, the diopter adjustment is only accurate for one person at a time, making it inconvenient to swap users during field observation. Additionally, a friend had to adjust the focus wheel to make the AR overlay sharp enough to read, a minor inconvenience noted during testing.

The reviewer has not yet tested the night mode due to cloudy skies but anticipates using the device for stargazing and teaching others about constellations. The Unistellar Envision is expected to receive additional functionality through future software updates, with a plan to allow third-party app development in 2027. The device offers distinct modes for night observation, daytime use, and navigation, the latter displaying cardinal direction alongside azimuth and elevation angles.
summary: I have been waiting to get my hands on a pair of Unistellar Envision smart binoculars since they were announced in 2024. Our editor-in-chief tried an early demo of them last year and said that they felt like something out of Star Trek.
author: Space.com

title: German astronomer discovers Tycho supernova in 1572, initially mistaken for a new star
content: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572, is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia, was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004. "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time. Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis, or the Blaze Star, the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). Is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
summary: German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova in the constellation Cassiopeia with the naked eye on Nov. 6, 1572, though Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. The event, known as Tycho's Star, was visible to the naked eye for 16 months and was not classified as a supernova until the 1940s.

title: Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook review – the heir to a legendary eatery … who sets soup on fire
content:
In the cooking series Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook, actor, rapper, and comedian Awkwafina navigates the kitchen with genuine bewilderment. Known by her real name, Nora Lum, within the series, she is portrayed as having no prior experience with culinary tools or techniques. The show documents her chaotic and humorous journey as she attempts to resurrect her family’s famous restaurant.

The review highlights the authenticity of Awkwafina’s lack of culinary knowledge, noting that her ignorance of how food, pans, knives, and plates work feels refreshing compared to other celebrity cooking shows where inexperience is often performed. Specific scenes illustrate her discomfort, including her crouched stance near the oven, her tentative handling of spatulas and ladles, and her visible aversion to raw ingredients.

The narrative describes her progression as chaotic, hilarious, and deeply moving. Despite her initial bafflement and fear of the kitchen environment, she valiantly works to restore the legacy of the eatery. The review concludes that her genuine inability to cook, rather than a staged act, provides a truthful and engaging foundation for the series.
summary: She is completely baffled in the kitchen, but the star valiantly resurrects her family’s famous restaurant. Her journey is chaotic, hilarious – and deeply moving It starts both very well and very badly does Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook.

title: U2 discuss new album Carnaval de Luz and Bono’s refusal to work with Trump
content: After some so-so albums, can U2’s new one, Carnaval de Luz, restore them to glory? They discuss male egos, working with Dolly Parton, and explain why, despite Trump, they still believe in democracy – at least in their band La Petite Maison, in Nice, has a certain reputation as a five-star celebrity haunt. Beyoncé eats here. So do Elton John, Tom Cruise, Harry Styles and Leonardo DiCaprio, their meals presided over by the restaurant’s founder, Nicole, variously described in print as “eccentric”, “unique” and “truculent” (she’s standing by the entrance when I arrive, and suffice to say, doesn’t look like someone you’d much enjoy being on the wrong side of). It’s enough of a celebrity haunt that the arrival of U2 – still incontrovertibly one of the biggest bands in the world 40 years after they could first reasonably have called themselves such – causes barely a murmur of interest among their fellow lunchtime diners. Then again, Bono is a regular. He was eating on the outdoor terrace the night of Nice’s terrorist attack, on Bastille Day in 2016, in which 86 people were killed. “I climbed through that window and hid under there,” he nods, pointing to a table at the rear of the restaurant. “Nicole,” he adds, “didn’t hide.”
summary: U2 discusses their new album, Carnaval de Luz, and explains why Bono cannot work with Donald Trump. The band also reflects on 50 years together and their continued belief in democracy within their group.

title: Macklemore says nine US arenas refused his Free Palestine tour
content:
Macklemore has claimed that nine major US arenas refused to host his Free Palestine fundraising tour, citing “intimidation, manipulation and suppression” in a social media post. The rapper stated that he intended to bring the tour to the United States but faced rejection from several prominent venues.

Among the locations named in his Instagram post are New York City’s Madison Square Garden, Los Angeles’s Crypto.com arena, and Brooklyn’s Barclays Center. Macklemore linked these refusals to the recent Ed Sheeran controversy, asserting that the venues declined to host his event.

title: Chilean director Sebastián Lelio, known for A Fantastic Woman, dies aged 52
content:
Sebastián Lelio, the Chilean director known for films such as Gloria and A Fantastic Woman, has died at the age of 52. The article describes him as a filmmaker of great passion and poetry who expertly captured both personal and political themes. Lelio is identified as one of the standard bearers of the Novisimo Cine Chileno, or New Chilean Cinema, a movement that includes directors Pablo Larraín, Patricio Guzmán, and Sebastián Silva.

The text notes that the last two decades have seen a significant rise in creativity from Chilean filmmakers. These directors brought global attention to the nation’s history, including the period of Augusto Pinochet’s rule, which the article characterizes as a tyranny enabled by the United States as an alternative to communism. The filmmakers also depicted the transition to a prosperous democratic normality where collective trauma and guilt persisted.

Lelio’s work is characterized as fierce, passionate, and sensual, with some films being explicitly political while others were not. The article argues that his films served as an expression of defiance against a system that deprived ordinary people of pleasure, effectively dramatizing the complex and conflicted zeitgeist of 21st-century Chile.
summary: Sebastián Lelio, the Chilean director of films including Gloria and A Fantastic Woman, has died at the age of 52. He was recognized for his passionate and sensual works that dramatized Chile's complex 21st-century zeitgeist.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd confirm split, reject WNBA draft influence claims
content:
Dallas Wings teammates Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd confirmed on Friday that they ended their romantic relationship more than a year ago. The former University of Connecticut teammates made the announcement during an episode of Fudd’s podcast, where they also addressed recent speculation. They specifically rejected claims that their personal relationship influenced the team’s decision to select Fudd with the No. 1 pick in this year’s WNBA draft.

In addition to clarifying the timeline of their split, the pair asked fans to stop sending hostile messages to them and their friends and family.
summary: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd confirmed on a podcast that they ended their romantic relationship more than a year ago. They rejected speculation that their relationship influenced the Dallas Wings' decision to select Fudd with the No. 1 pick in the WNBA draft.

title: Wallabies struggle to turn moments into momentum despite talented squad
content:
The Wallabies possess a squad with the potential for exceptional performances, yet questions persist regarding their ability to consistently translate individual talent into sustained team success. The team frequently demonstrates moments of brilliance, such as Len Ikitau’s underhand pass to Max Jorgensen for a late try at Twickenham and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii’s run past multiple British and Irish Lions defenders. Additionally, Australia has shown resilience in high-pressure situations, including securing a victory against the Springboks while down to 11 men and defending a four-point lead with five minutes remaining.

Despite these flashes of ability, the Wallabies have struggled to maintain this level of performance over extended periods. Historical context suggests that while previous Australian teams have exhibited similar sparks, few have managed to convert them into consistent wins across consecutive matches. Recent results reflect this inconsistency, as the team lost all four Tests on their European tour last autumn and suffered two additional defeats in the summer.

Following a successful unbeaten run of six matches against Italy, Japan, Argentina, and South Africa, the Wallabies faced significant setbacks in the Bledisloe Cup. They were defeated by the All Blacks in consecutive matches, losing by 31 points in one week and 22 points the following week. These results highlight the ongoing challenge for the team to turn isolated moments of excellence into lasting momentum and revive the spirits of the squad.
summary: The Wallabies possess individual talents capable of magic, but doubts remain about their ability to form a consistently winning team. Australia’s recent form includes losing all four European Tests and two consecutive Bledisloe Cup matches to the All Blacks.

title: Tuchel calls Jobe Bellingham to England squad after Jude's request
content: Jude had asked head coach to scout Dortmund midfielder ‘It will be beautiful for Jude to have his brother close’ Thomas Tuchel has given a first England call-up to Jobe Bellingham, admitting the midfielder’s older brother, Jude, had nagged him to do so, as he set up the prospect of their family dream being realised. Tuchel’s inclusion of the younger Bellingham for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain was further evidence of his shift away from the squad that served him well at the World Cup last summer and towards a fresh dynamic for the mission to win Euro 2028. The manager has named a 25-man group for the game against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday and the one against Spain in Madrid three days after; of the 22 outfield players, only 11 were at the World Cup.
summary: Thomas Tuchel has selected Jobe Bellingham for England's upcoming Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain. The manager admitted that Jude Bellingham had asked him to scout his younger brother, describing their potential reunion as a beautiful story.

title: Keenan hat-trick leads Ireland to 42-12 win over Argentina
content:
Ireland secured an emphatic 42-12 victory over Argentina in the Nations Championship, with Keenan scoring a hat-trick in a match that featured six tries for the Irish side. The result marked a significant win for Ireland as they opened November’s international window. In contrast, Argentina’s defeat was highlighted by Carreras, who scored twice for his team during the encounter.

The match was described as almost tame, a notable shift from the historically mean and nasty World Cup meetings between the two nations. Although the rivalry has never been friendly, ranging from uncapped affairs to full Test status, this particular contest lacked the previous intensity. The backdrop for the game included next year’s World Cup in Australia, where there is a decent chance of the two teams meeting again in the knockout stages. Should that scenario occur, Ireland will view complacency as their biggest enemy.
summary: Ireland defeated Argentina 42-12 in a Nations Championship match where Keenan scored a hat-trick. Argentina's Carreras scored twice during the defeat.

title: Thierno Barry scores twice as Everton beat Coventry
content:
Thierno Barry scored twice to lead Everton to a comeback victory over Coventry, securing the club’s third consecutive win. The striker’s second goal, which appeared to come off his arm, took his season total to 10 goals in all competitions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added a late goal to seal the result in convincing style.

The match featured two strong penalty shouts for Coventry that were dismissed, resulting in a torturous night for manager Frank Lampard against his old club. Despite a calamitous transfer window, Everton currently sits fifth in the Premier League, with Barry positioned just behind Erling Haaland in the goalscoring chart.
summary: Thierno Barry scored two goals to help Everton secure a comeback victory against Coventry. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added a late goal to seal Everton's third consecutive win.

title: England rugby faces injury crisis and Borthwick scrutiny ahead of Australia match
content:
England rugby faces a familiar pre-season challenge as injury concerns and questions surrounding head coach Steve Borthwick resurface ahead of the Nations Championship opener against Australia. The article notes that cracks in the relationship between the players and their head coach have begun to appear, a recurring theme for the team during this time of year.

The squad is currently dealing with significant absences due to injuries sustained on the Bagshot training pitch. Tom Curry, Alex Mitchell, and Archie McParland are all out, while Guy Pepper, Benhard van Rensburg, Sam Underhill, Kepu Tuipulotu, and Chandler Cunningham-South are also unavailable. These missing players have left the team with less energy and dynamism than expected.

The piece suggests that Sunday’s hosts must stop seeking excuses and instead focus on what they can control. As crowds gather at Twickenham, uncertainty remains about what to expect from the match, with the team preparing to face a battle-hardened Australian side.
summary: England's squad is missing several key players, including Tom Curry, Alex Mitchell, and Archie McParland, due to injuries sustained on the training pitch. The team must overcome these absences and questions about head coach Steve Borthwick to begin the Nations Championship against Australia.

title: Mother and baby's immune cells linked to aggressive placental inflammation in preterm cases
content:
Researchers led by Nardhy Gomez-Lopez, a professor of obstetrics and gynecology and of pathology and immunology at WashU Medicine, investigated the cellular drivers of chronic placental inflammation. This condition can occur when the maternal immune response, which typically prevents fetal rejection, becomes dysregulated. The study specifically examined the immune cell landscape at the junction connecting the mother and fetus in pregnancies affected by this complication.

To map these immune cells, the team utilized spatial and single-cell gene and protein expression profiling. This approach allowed them to analyze the placenta down to individual cells, providing detailed insights into the aggressive inflammation associated with preterm cases.
summary: In a healthy pregnancy, a finely tuned maternal immune response prevents the mother's body from rejecting the growing fetus. But in some pregnancies, this response goes haywire, leading to a potentially dangerous complication known as chronic placental inflammation.

title: MIT's CheMeleon model predicts molecular behavior from scant data
content:
A new method developed at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) demonstrates that artificial intelligence can outperform existing approaches for predicting molecular behavior when data on specific properties is limited. This development addresses the trial-and-error nature of discovering new molecules for pharmaceuticals, electronics, and energy sectors, where perfect prediction of chemical compound behavior remains elusive. The findings were published in the Sept. 14 issue of the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling by MIT graduate student Akshat Shirish Zalte, recent graduate Jackson Burns PhD ’26, Research Scientist Charlles Abreu, Professor William Green, and three researchers from BASF.

The open-source model, named CheMeleon, was built using ChemProp, a machine-learning package developed and maintained by the Green group at MIT. CheMeleon is a pre-trained foundation model that utilizes molecular descriptors of one million molecules from PubChem, a freely available chemical database maintained by the U.S. National Institutes of Health. By pre-training on this extensive dataset, the model learns correlations between molecular structure and a catalog of approximately 1,600 descriptors developed by chemists. This process allows the system to identify underlying patterns and relationships, enabling it to apply this general chemical understanding to new, unknown molecules even when fine-tuned with only a few data points for a specific task.

Professor William Green, the Hoyt Hottel Professor of Chemical Engineering at MIT, noted the model’s impact following a contest organized by OpenADMET earlier this year to predict properties of unsynthesized molecules. When the winners were announced, nine of the top 20 entries had utilized CheMeleon in their process. This success led to inquiries from pharmaceutical companies before the paper had even undergone peer review. Green stated that at least one pharmaceutical company adopted CheMeleon as its new company policy for initial molecular modeling decisions, instructing its staff to start with the tool when modeling any property.

Akshat Shirish Zalte explained that unlike many deep-learning models that require extensive data from published literature, CheMeleon does not rely on literature sources. Instead, it calculates molecular descriptors such as molecular weight and the number of oxygens. The team compared CheMeleon against other foundation models and classical expert-driven models across 58 test cases. Zalte reported that CheMeleon performed best in these comparisons. Green added that the model drastically reduces the number of molecules requiring experimental testing, offering a significant advantage given that synthesizing and testing large numbers of molecules is both slow and expensive.

The research team included Jochen Sieg, Christian Feldmann, and Miriam Mathea, researchers at BASF SE in Germany. The work was supported by the Machine Learning for Pharmaceutical Discovery and Synthesis consortium, as well as fellowship support from the U.S. Department of Energy and MathWorks. An earlier version of the paper has been available online since last year, and the model is accessible for download and fine-tuning through ChemProp.
summary: Researchers at MIT developed CheMeleon, a pre-trained foundation model that uses molecular descriptors from a million compounds to predict chemical properties with high accuracy. The open-source model outperformed other methods in 58 test cases and has been adopted by pharmaceutical companies to reduce the number of molecules requiring expensive experimental testing.

title: Is 'ferritin face' real? Experts explain iron deficiency signs
content: Social media is awash with claims iron deficiency can be identified in the mirror by dark circles, breaking hair and dry skin. But is ‘ferritin face’ real? Madeleine Finlay tells Ian Sample why so many of us struggle to keep our iron levels up, how we can actually diagnose low iron and the best way to correct a deficiency, with help from Hal Drakesmith, a professor of iron biology at Oxford University, and advice from Dr Sue Pavord, a consultant haematologist at Oxford university hospitals and associate senior lecturer in clinical medicine at St Edmund Hall.
summary: Social media claims that iron deficiency causes dark circles, hair loss, and dry skin, but experts question if this 'ferritin face' is real. Madeleine Finlay discusses how to diagnose and correct low iron with help from Oxford University professors and consultants.

title: LDraw Mecha: Agents Infer LEGO Mechanisms from Source and Animate Them
content:
A developer has released LDraw Mecha, a new agentic tool designed to animate LEGO models by inferring their mechanical structures from source code. The project builds on the creator’s previous release, LDraw Nova, which generates LDraw source code for assembling LEGO CAD models. Following community interest in animated AI-generated LEGO models, the developer explored using agentic large language models to reverse-engineer mechanisms within existing LDraw files.

LDraw Mecha operates by reading specially annotated LDraw source files to infer the model’s structure and identify specific submodels that function as mechanisms. The system then plans animations for these components and executes them using Blender. The final output is a rigged and animated version of the original model, exported as a Blender (.blend) file.

The project is currently at version 0.5.0, with a public repository, gallery, and process documentation available on GitHub. The creator has shared the work on Hacker News, seeking community feedback on this unusual application of agentic AI in 3D animation.
summary: Hi there :) Around a month ago, I released LDraw Nova, an agentic toolset for assembling LEGO CAD models by generating LDraw source code files. For more details, here's the Show HN post: https://news.

title: AI data center expansion faces bipartisan backlash, polls, and new regulatory restrictions
content:
Massive new data centers serve as the physical foundation for the artificial intelligence ambitions of major technology companies, yet their rapid expansion has sparked global conflicts regarding power grids, utility bills, and environmental impacts. Data centers emerged as a significant bipartisan issue ahead of the 2026 midterms, with voters largely opposing expansion at the polls. In the aftermath of the election, Democratic leaders are calling for further restrictions and slowdowns, while tech giants like OpenAI and Amazon promise to collaborate more closely with local communities and cover their own energy costs.

The political landscape surrounding these facilities has shifted dramatically, with data centers influencing the outcome of several key races. Maine Republican Susan Collins conceded her Senate seat in a tech-fueled race, while a Democrat was projected to win an Ohio seat that Republicans warned could pose problems for data center development. Additionally, Texas, a state dense with data centers, turned blue in the election. Following these results, a lame-duck Congress is considering measures to speed up energy projects, while New York became the first state to enact a data center moratorium.

Environmental and community concerns have intensified, with reports indicating that data centers could send US climate pollution skyrocketing and erase decades of air quality gains. Specific regions are facing distinct challenges; for instance, AI infrastructure is straining Arizona’s water supply, and Amazon’s data centers used 2.5 billion gallons of water last year. In Utah, a 40,000-acre data center project was approved despite community outcry, and Kevin O’Leary agreed to downsize a massive project in the state. Meanwhile, in Indiana, the mayor of Shelbyville stated that only people living in “shitty houses” oppose data centers, while Amazon employees have reported facing termination for backing data center limits.

Tech companies are responding to these pressures through various strategic moves. OpenAI has begun renaming its facilities “compute campuses” and is stepping back from non-disclosure agreements for its projects. Nvidia has guaranteed up to $105 billion to support an OpenAI data center, while Anthropic is paying $15 billion a year for access to Elon Musk’s data centers. Other major players, including Google, Meta, and Microsoft, are pursuing diverse energy solutions, such as nuclear power, geothermal energy, and vehicle-to-grid technology, to manage the immense power demands of their infrastructure.

The debate has also extended to unconventional locations and infrastructure. Elon Musk has proposed merging SpaceX and xAI to build data centers in space, a concept Google and Amazon have also explored. On the ground, the construction boom has led to a surge in gas projects to power data centers, with the Department of Justice arguing that XAI’s gas-powered facility is necessary for national security. As the industry expands, utility companies are promising to spare consumers from the full cost of AI’s energy bill, while regulators in California and other states tighten rules on energy and water usage.
summary: Voters largely opposed data center expansion in the 2026 midterms, leading Democratic leaders to call for further restrictions and slowdowns. Tech companies are responding by promising to cover energy costs and work more closely with local communities.
author: The Verge

title: KPop Demon Hunters 4K Blu-ray drops to $24.99 at Amazon and Barnes & Noble
content:
The 4K Blu-ray version of the animated film KPop Demon Hunters is currently available for $24.99 at Amazon and Barnes & Noble, a significant discount from its original $49.95 price. This price point is lower than the $26.99 monthly cost of a Netflix Premium subscription, which some viewers maintain primarily to watch the film in 4K. While the deal was previously available for in-store pickup at Barnes & Noble, it is now accessible online at both retailers.

The release also includes a recently launched Criterion Collection edition, which features a 4K digital master with Dolby Vision HDR and Dolby Atmos sound. This set contains two standard 1080p Blu-rays: one with the film and another dedicated to special features, including a feature-length animatic, a making-of documentary, and lyric videos. The package also includes physical items such as collectible postcards and an essay by Polygon alum Karen Han.

title: SpaceX aims to become major mobile carrier with 5G network and Boost Mobile talks
content: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network here on Earth. As part of its plans to rival AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, SpaceX has inked a deal with Qualcomm, which will deploy its cellular technology across tens of thousands of 5G cell sites starting in 2027. SpaceX is also reportedly in talks to buy Boost Mobile, potentially allowing it to launch Starlink Mobile through the service. Another report suggests SpaceX may tap into 80,000 cell sites across the US to build out its network. SpaceX’s big plans have garnered some reactions in the telecom industry. Tim Höttges, the CEO of T-Mobile’s parent company Deutsche Telekom, said he takes SpaceX’s plans “super serious” but that it could cost Musk more than $200 billion to pull off. Follow along for the latest updates on Starlink’s major mobile carrier ambitions. What will it take for SpaceX to launch its “major” mobile network? SpaceX is working with Qualcomm to build its Starlink Mobile 5G network SpaceX could buy Boost Mobile as part of its big mobile carrier plans SpaceX’s mobile carrier push reportedly involves tapping into 80,000 cell sites SpaceX announces plan to become a ‘major mobile carrier’ SpaceX is coming for T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon
summary: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network here on Earth.

title: “Does Meta think we can’t read?” Meta abandons sketchy commercial terms update.
content: After weeks of backlash —and a failed attempt to quell it —Meta has indefinitely delayed plans to update its commercial terms and require Meta Business account users to allow extensive AI training on external websites linked on Facebook. "We're pausing the ‌changes ⁠as we continue to engage with stakeholders and ​take ​our ⁠time to get this right. ​In the ​meantime, ⁠our existing terms remain in ⁠effect," a Meta spokesperson told Reuters. Soon after Meta notified business account holders of the upcoming changes, legal experts warned Nieman Lab that the vague language could allow the company to ignore scraping preferences specified in robots. Txt files and exhaustively crawl vast amounts of off-Facebook content for AI training. Since virtually every news publisher has a Facebook page, Nieman Lab sounded the alarm that Meta could potentially avoid millions in licensing fees if the TOS update happened as planned. Read full article Comments
summary: “Does Meta think we can’t read?” Meta abandons sketchy commercial terms update.

title: AST SpaceMobile to Develop Medium‑Lift Rocket Blacklift to Expand Market
content: There are optimistic plans for spaceflight, and then there are optimistic plans. AST SpaceMobile is a Texas-based, publicly traded company building very large satellites to provide direct-to-cell communications on Earth. But it has been having trouble finding rides to space. So on Friday, AST announced that it is developing a medium-lift rocket, named Blacklift, which will have the capacity to lift 20 metric tons to low-Earth orbit. Oh, and the company said it would start launching commercially in late 2028. "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owner's economics in the industry," said Abel Avellan, founder, chairman, and CEO of AST SpaceMobile, in a news release. Read full article Comments
summary: AST SpaceMobile, a Texas‑based publicly traded company, announced it is developing the Blacklift medium‑lift rocket with a 20‑metric‑ton capacity to low‑Earth orbit. The company plans to begin commercial launches in late 2028, aiming to secure regular, unconstrained access to orbit and improve its economics.
author: Ars Technica

title: John Wick creator Chad Stahelski returns with dystopian action film Karōshi
content: Those of us missing the John Wick universe can take heart, because Chad Stahelski—who created that franchise—is coming back early next year with a new dystopian action film. It's called Karōshi (a Japanese term that means "death overwork"), and Lionsgate released a killer trailer that puts this film at the top of my list of "must see" movies of 2027. Dying from working too hard is a very real phenomenon, not just in Japan and much of Asia, but also in Sweden. The physical cause is usually stress-related heart attacks or strokes, as well as suicide ( karōjisatsu in Japan). Writer/director Takashi Doscher has transported that concept to a grim, futuristic corporate Manhattan, specifically a company called Ikigai Technologies. Per the official premise: Karōshi is an action-thriller set in a near-future Manhattan, where corporate loyalty and cultural tradition have reshaped everyday life. When a mysterious outsider infiltrates a powerful company after a worker’s death, he exposes the violent system hidden beneath its polished surface. Teo Yoo ( Past Lives ) stars as the aptly named Hiro, who is clearly out for vengeance against the offending corporation. The cast also includes Takehiro Hira, so memorable in the 2024 miniseries Shōgun, as well as Giancarlo Esposito, Cynthia Erivo, Bill Camp, Richard Harmon, Isabel May, and Show Kasamatsu. Read full article Comments
summary: Chad Stahelski, creator of the John Wick franchise, is returning with the dystopian action film Karōshi, set in a near‑future Manhattan corporate environment. The film, written and directed by Takashi Doscher, stars Teo Yoo, Takehiro Hira, Giancarlo Esposito, Cynthia Erivo, Bill Camp, Richard Harmon, Isabel May, and Show Kasamatsu.
author: Ars Technica

title: FAA to ditch floppy disks in historic air traffic control upgrade
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration announced that it will discontinue the use of floppy disks in its air‑traffic control system. The agency said the move is part of a long‑awaited modernization effort that will give controllers faster access to data needed for safety alerts.

The upgrade involves installing the new Enterprise Information Display System (E‑IDS) in 435 facilities, replacing several older information display systems that date back to the 1980s. According to the FAA, the new system will replace floppy disks that hold vital weather and other critical information with a streamlined, 21st‑century solution.

E‑IDS will be deployed to operational control positions at more than 400 facilities across all air‑traffic control domains. The FAA said the system will provide operationally essential information for controlling aircraft.
summary: The FAA will stop using floppy disks as part of a long‑awaited upgrade that will give air‑traffic controllers faster access to safety‑alert data. The new Enterprise Information Display System will be installed in 435 facilities, replacing older display systems that date to the 1980s.
author: Ars Technica

title: Roku to remove Aquatic Life screensaver effective December 1
content:
Roku OS users will lose access to the “Aquatic Life” screensaver as of December 1, following the termination of a licensing agreement. Affected users reported receiving device alerts this week notifying them of the change, a development first covered by Cord Cutters News. The screensaver, also known as the Marine Aquarium, has been available to Roku OS users for ten years.

The content indicates that the developer ended the lucrative deal because Fox acquired Roku. Previously, Roku licensed the animation from artist Jim Sachs through Prolific Publishing.
summary: Roku will no longer offer the Aquatic Life screensaver to Roku OS users after December 1. The screensaver, known as Marine Aquarium, had been licensed from artist Jim Sachs via Prolific Publishing for 10 years.

title: Nvidia hardware worth $11.4 M disappears en route from Oakland to Texas
content:
A shipment of Nvidia hardware worth $11.4 million disappeared while being transported from Oakland to Texas. According to The Mercury News, six pallets of unknown Nvidia equipment left Oakland on August 29 in a truck bound for Fort Worth, Texas. The truck, bearing the logo of a food‑transportation company, was scheduled to pick up the cargo and then vanish from the grid.

The theft was not discovered until early September, when the buyers realized the shipment had never arrived. Police tracing the truck’s route found it made several multi‑hour stops after picking up the hardware before the vehicle was lost somewhere in San Bernardino County, California.

Oakland police confirmed that a grand theft report was filed on September 13 and that the investigation remains ongoing. Authorities have not disclosed the specific Nvidia hardware that was stolen or the exact method of the theft.
summary: Nvidia hardware worth $11.4 M disappears en route from Oakland to Texas.
author: Ars Technica

title: Earth's Mantle Movements May Explain Great Unconformity Gap
content: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. "This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth's mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet's interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says. Read full article Comments
summary: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top.
author: Ars Technica

title: Chainalysis reports hackers stole credentials and tokens for all customers
content:
Chainalysis, a blockchain analysis firm, announced that hackers have obtained sensitive personal information for all of its users following a breach of its network security. The stolen data includes names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens. The firm listed a number of high‑profile customers, such as the FBI, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the U.S. Air Force, Microsoft, Coinbase, and Barclays. It is unclear whether the theft exposes these customers to additional threats.

The company said the incident occurred in October and was similar to other hacks that month. An external actor used AI‑agent‑assisted offensive techniques to gain unauthorized access to Chainalysis systems and internal tools. In an email to affected customers, Chainalysis noted that “non‑sensitive customer data, such as user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels for users provisioned on our platform were accessed.” The firm has not explained why it classified this information as non‑sensitive.
summary: Chainalysis said hackers obtained names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all its users after a breach. The incident, which used AI‑agent‑assisted techniques, impacted customers such as the FBI, ICE, US Air Force, Microsoft, Coinbase and Barclays.
author: Ars Technica

content: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion in a funding round that has not yet closed. The round is expected to close in the coming weeks, and the company’s valuation is reported at $1.25 trillion.

title: The nine best personalized gift ideas: customized for the person you love
content:
The article titled “The nine best personalized gift ideas: customized for the person you love” emphasizes how monogramming or customizing elevates a present. It argues that a personalized gift shows the giver knows what the recipient likes and who they are, making the gesture feel more intentional.

It notes that “gift math” suggests offering a personalized item earns extra points, because monogramming or engraving requires time and effort. This effort can make a gift feel more meaningful than a last‑minute grocery‑store bouquet of carnations.

The piece highlights that a personalized gift signals foresight and consideration, delivering thoughtfulness without being overbearing. It concludes by saying the ideas presented are drawn from suggestions the author has given, received, and truly loves.
summary: The article explains that personalized gifts, such as monogramming or engraving, show recipients that the giver knows their likes and identity, and can earn extra points according to “Gift math”. It also notes that personalized gifts convey foresight and consideration, making them more meaningful than last‑minute generic gifts.

title: Democrats and Sanders Renew Calls for Datacenter Moratoriums After Midterm Victory
content:
Several newly elected Democrats and Senator Bernie Sanders have renewed calls for datacenter moratoriums in the days after the U.S. midterm elections. The sweeping Democratic victory, which was buoyed in part by backlash to the tech industry, has added momentum to efforts to slow the multi‑trillion‑dollar buildout of controversial facilities that are intended to power artificial intelligence.

On the social‑media platform X, Sanders posted a call for an immediate national datacenter moratorium this week. “Americans don’t want Big Tech oligarchs wrecking the environment, gutting jobs and threatening humanity’s future,” he said on Wednesday. The tech industry fears that such delays could impede its multi‑trillion‑dollar infrastructure buildout.
summary: Several newly elected Democrats and Senator Bernie Sanders have renewed calls for datacenter moratoriums following the US midterm elections. Sanders posted on X a call for an immediate national datacenter moratorium, warning that Americans don’t want Big Tech oligarchs wrecking the environment, gutting jobs and threatening humanity’s future.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Apple’s Grey List Blocks Over 100,000 Words From iPhone Predictive Text
content: There are more than 100,000 words and phrases that the tech giant has restricted its predictive text from completing, research shows “Australia is a very bad place to question your sexuality on MDMA with NSA spies” might be a text you would wish to send to your friends, if you have had an extraordinarily complicated night out in Sydney. But your iPhone won’t help you spell any of it if you try to swipe-type it – that is, by gliding a finger across a keyboard as opposed to pecking out a word.
summary: Apple has restricted more than 100,000 words and phrases from its predictive text. The iPhone will not spell or complete these words when swipe‑typing.

title: US tech stocks plunge as investors fear AI slowdown after midterm elections
content: After Thursday’s share‑price plunge on Wall Street, market participants are questioning whether the resulting volatility could signal the beginning of a large market downturn. The article notes that global financial markets have entered a tailspin as investors bet on an AI slowdown following the U.S. midterm elections. It also points out that this is not the first time stock markets have wobbled in recent months amid concerns over a tech bubble. The piece ends by asking whether this volatility might herald a significant market collapse.
summary: Thursday’s share price plunge on Wall Street sent US tech stocks lower. Investors are betting on an AI slowdown after the US midterm elections, contributing to a global market tailspin.

title: Five rescued off Kiribati after months drifting; Chuuk governor in talks to return them
content: Five people were rescued off Kiribati after spending months drifting at sea. Chuuk state governor Alexander Narruhn said in a Sunday statement that he is in talks with the Kiribati government to arrange the survivors’ return home.
summary: Five people were rescued off Kiribati after months drifting at sea. Chuuk state governor Alexander Narruhn said he is in talks with the Kiribati government to bring the survivors home.

title: Thousands gather on Regent Street for London Christmas lights switch‑on
content: Thousands of people assembled on Regent Street in London on Thursday, 5 November, to mark the start of the Christmas season. The gathering featured a spectacular lights switch‑on ceremony accompanied by a fireworks display, celebrating the famous shopping destination’s holiday festivities.
summary: Thousands of people gathered on Regent Street in London on Thursday, 5 November. The event featured a Christmas lights switch‑on and a fireworks display to mark the start of the season.

content:
An Azerbaijani delegation, led by its energy minister, travelled to Ukraine to sign a 2026‑2027 Action Plan.  

The bilateral talks focused on emergency winter grid equipment, joint manufacturing, and expanding European transit via the Trans‑Balkan route.
summary: An Azerbaijani delegation led by its energy minister travelled to Ukraine to sign a 2026-2027 Action Plan. Bilateral talks focused on emergency winter grid equipment, joint manufacturing, and expanding European transit via the Trans-Balkan route.

title: China watches US midterms as Democrats gain Congress, Trump becomes lame‑duck
content:
The recent U.S. midterm elections have seen the Democratic Party take control of both the House and Senate, leaving President Donald Trump in a lame‑duck position for the remainder of his term.

Professor Steve Tsang of the SOAS China Institute told France 24 that a weakened Trump could give Beijing a stronger negotiating position, but that Chinese leadership recognizes that Congress has limited influence on foreign policy and wants to keep warm personal ties between the two presidents.
summary: China watches US midterms as Democrats gain Congress, Trump becomes lame‑duck.

title: Trump's Midterm Loss Leaves Zelensky Optimistic About US Support for Ukraine
content: The Republican Party suffered a crushing defeat in the recent midterm elections, a result that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described as leaving him optimistic about continued support for Kyiv and stronger transatlantic ties. However, with U.S. President Donald Trump retaining broad foreign‑policy powers, the Democratic majority in Congress may have limited ability to enact substantial changes.
summary: The Republican Party's crushing defeat in the midterm elections has made Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky optimistic about future support for Kyiv and stronger transatlantic relations. However, because US President Donald Trump retains broad foreign policy powers, the Democratic majority in Congress may have limited scope to bring about substantial change.

title: Sen. Jon Ossoff emerges as Democratic frontrunner prospect after Georgia midterm win
content:
Following a resounding midterm victory in Georgia—a former Republican stronghold—39‑year‑old Senator Jon Ossoff has emerged as a prominent figure as the Democratic Party looks ahead to 2028 for its next presidential nominee.  

Ossoff’s natural confidence, polished media performances, and ability to appeal to a diverse electorate have prompted comparisons with Barack Obama.  

Despite the excitement surrounding his national prospects, the question remains whether political momentum in the Senate necessarily translates into a presidential frontrunner.
summary: Senator Jon Ossoff, 39, gained prominence after a resounding midterm victory in Georgia, a former Republican stronghold. Democrats are looking toward 2028 for their next presidential nominee, but it is unclear if his Senate momentum will make him a frontrunner.
author: France 24

title: Midterm Fallout Reviewed After Worst Republican Win Since 1970s; Groups Plan Protests
content: A World This Week ‘Mid Terms Special’ Gavin Lee is joined by panel of four distinguished international correspondents to assess the aftermath of the worst Republican election result since the 1970s, post Watergate. We ask, is peak MAGA over? What will now change at home and abroad? And who ends the week in pole position as Presidential frontrunner for 2028? We also consider the scale and scope of Europe Wide Protests: This week housing organisations, trade unions and activist groups from seven countries met in Paris issuing a joint call for demonstrations. Are the national protest movements becoming a coordinated European movement?

title: Trump names immigration hardliner Stephen Miller as chief of staff
content: President Donald Trump announced on Friday that advisor Stephen Miller will become his new chief of staff. Miller, who has been instrumental in the administration’s mass‑deportation program, has faced particular criticism following the January shooting deaths of two Minneapolis protesters by ICE agents.
summary: Trump announced on Friday that advisor Stephen Miller will become his new chief of staff. Miller has been instrumental in the administration's mass deportation programme and faced criticism after ICE agents shot two Minneapolis protesters in January.

title: Pope Leo lands in Uruguay to start 12‑day South America tour
content: Pope Leo arrived in Uruguay on Friday, marking the start of a 12‑day South American tour that will also include visits to Argentina and Peru. The itinerary is noted as a homecoming for the pontiff, who spent nearly twenty years living in Peru and holds both U.S. and Peruvian citizenship.
summary: Pope Leo touched down in Uruguay on Friday to begin a 12‑day tour that will also include Argentina and Peru. The tour is seen as a homecoming because he lived in Peru for almost two decades and holds joint US and Peruvian citizenship.
author: France 24

title: Europe bomb hoaxes widen
content:
The Irish government says a series of hoax bomb scares sent to several Irish media outlets and European airlines appears to be part of a coordinated campaign of disruption. Dozens of commercial flights have been targeted by email threats described as more specific than typical hoaxes.

Ireland’s broadcaster RTE evacuated its premises this morning, and several Italian airlines reported receiving a message that claimed to be from a Russian extremist group called the Fighters of the Male State, which denied any involvement. France 24’s Jean‑Emile Jammine interviewed Eric Schouten, founder and CEO of Dyami Security Intelligence, about the incidents.
summary: The series of hoax bomb scares sent to several Irish media outlets and European airlines are likely part of a coordinated campaign of disruption, according to the Irish government. Dozens of commercial flights have been targetted by email with threats said to be over and above the typical hoax in specificty.
author: France 24

title: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie sentenced to 200 years for killing 190 children
content:
Cult leader Paul Mackenzie was sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murder of 190 children who were starved to death on his orders.  

Activists in South Africa warn that new data centres could add pressure to already strained water and electricity supplies. Senegal continues to celebrate the spirit of sport at the Youth Olympic Games.
summary: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie was sentenced to 200 years in prison for ordering the starvation deaths of 190 children. The sentencing was announced in tonight's edition.

title: Critics urge Democrats to probe Trump's Middle East deals in corruption investigations
content: After winning the U.S. midterm elections, Democrats said they will investigate corruption in the Trump administration. Critics have urged that the inquiry should include the former president’s Middle‑East deals as a focus of any future corruption investigations.

title: Ueno Bank collapse triggers political crisis in Paraguay
content: Paraguay is in serious crisis after the sudden collapse of Ueno Bank, which authorities suspect involved financial fraud that puts public money at risk and affects millions of customers. The fallout has led to President Santiago Pena facing impeachment.
summary: Paraguay is in serious crisis after the sudden collapse of Ueno Bank amid suspected financial fraud and risk to public money. President Santiago Pena is facing impeachment.

title: Afghanistan faces deepening humanitarian crisis as sweeping rights curbs worsen
content: Afghanistan is described by a senior United Nations official as being at a “difficult crossroad” more than five years after the Taliban’s return to power. While relative stability and security persist, they are being eroded by a fragile economy, sweeping curbs on rights and acute humanitarian need.
summary: A senior UN official said on Friday that Afghanistan is at a “difficult crossroad” more than five years after the Taliban returned to power. Relative stability and security are being undercut by a fragile economy, sweeping curbs on rights and acute humanitarian need.

title: Scientists find pink noise makes conversations more enjoyable
content:
A recent study finds that the most enjoyable conversations strike a balance between exploring a topic and pulling in fresh ideas.  

Cicero, in an early attempt at conversation rules, advised watching tone, avoiding boredom, keeping temper in check, and not rambling—especially about oneself.  

Scientists, following Cicero's guidance, have identified a telltale signature of a satisfying exchange: a healthy dose of pink noise.
summary: A study found that the most enjoyable conversations balance exploring a topic with introducing fresh ideas. Researchers say the secret to a mutually satisfying exchange is a healthy dose of pink noise.
author: Guardian World

title: Russell Brand faces sentencing as police suspect attacks on at least 10 women
content:
Met police chief has stated that “many more” victims of Russell Brand could come forward, as the actor and comedian awaits sentencing. Police are bracing for at least 10 other women who are suspected of having been attacked by the disgraced star.

Brand, 51, is scheduled to be sentenced on Monday to what is expected to be a lengthy jail sentence for rape and sexual assaults. The report notes that he abused his fame to become a “predator” targeting women and got away with it for years.
summary: Met police chief said many more victims could come forward as Russell Brand, 51, awaits sentencing. Police suspect he attacked at least 10 women and he is expected to receive a lengthy jail term for rape and sexual assaults.
author: Guardian World

title: Russell Brand's barrister Ian Winter KC reports himself to regulator after tirade
content:
Ian Winter KC, the barrister representing Russell Brand, has reported himself to his professional regulator following an incident involving a journalist. The report was made after Winter was accused of launching a tirade at Rosamund Urwin of the Sunday Times shortly after Brand was found guilty of rape.

Winter “confronted” Urwin, whose investigative work led to Brand’s victims coming forward, and told her, “I hope you are pleased with yourself.” The barrister’s self-report to the watchdog marks a formal step in addressing the alleged clash between the legal representative and the press.
summary: Ian Winter KC, Russell Brand’s barrister, reported himself to his professional regulator after being accused of confronting Sunday Times journalist Rosamund Urwin. He told Urwin, whose investigation led to Brand’s victims coming forward, “I hope you are pleased with yourself.”
author: Guardian World

title: Three men charged in US for AI‑based CEO impersonation scheme stealing over $100m
content:
Three men have been charged in the United States for a scheme that used artificial‑intelligence technology to impersonate corporate executives. An indictment that was recently unsealed by the U.S. Department of Justice alleges that the defendants—Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan, and Guy Sheetrit—altered voices and images of CEOs and attorneys to convince employees at various companies to send large payments. The indictment claims the fraud resulted in the theft of more than $100 million.

According to a press release from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York, Soall and Hazan were arrested in Spain during the summer, while Sheetrit was arrested in the United Kingdom in September. The alleged fraudulent activity is said to have occurred between 2024 and 2026. The case is currently pending in U.S. federal court.
summary: Three men charged in US for AI‑based CEO impersonation scheme stealing over $100m.
author: Guardian World

title: Thomas Markle arrested in Florida, charged with child sexual abuse material possession
content:
Father of the Duchess of Sussex, Thomas Markle, was arrested by U.S. federal agents in Florida and charged with possession of child sexual abuse material, according to the Federal Bureau of Investigation. The 82‑year‑old was taken into custody at a senior‑care facility in Polk County early on Friday and appeared briefly in federal court in Tampa later that afternoon.

After the initial court appearance, Markle was released under the condition that he be electronically monitored. The Associated Press reported the arrest and the subsequent release terms.

The notice includes a list of resources for reporting child abuse and seeking support. In the United States, callers can reach the Childhelp abuse hotline at 800‑422‑4453. In the United Kingdom, the NSPCC provides assistance at 0800 1111 for children and 0808 800 5000 for concerned adults. Additional support contacts are provided for Australia and for adult survivors of childhood abuse.
summary: Thomas Markle, 82, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, was arrested by US federal agents in Florida and charged with possession of child sexual abuse material. He was taken into custody at a senior care facility in Polk County, made a brief appearance in federal court in Tampa, and was released with electronic monitoring.
author: Guardian World

title: Activists break into Microsoft datacentre construction site in Amsterdam
content:
Activists stormed the construction site of a Microsoft data centre in Westpoort, Amsterdam. The breach formed part of a broader series of actions across Europe that protest the social and environmental impacts of the AI boom.

Protesters identified as members of the Dutch direct‑action group Geef Tegengas clashed with police while entering the site. Some participants climbed a crane, ignited flares and attached helium balloons to equipment during the demonstration.
summary: Protesters from the Dutch direct‑action group Geef Tegengas stormed the Microsoft datacentre construction site at Westpoort in Amsterdam, clashing with police. Several activists climbed a crane, lit flares and tied helium balloons to equipment.
author: Guardian World

title: 34 Primary Students Reach NSW Premier’s Spelling Bee Finals After Beating 200,000
content:
Primary school students who out‑performed 200,000 competitors across New South Wales have advanced to the Premier’s Spelling Bee finals in Sydney. The finals were held on Friday afternoon in a small theatre hall in Sydney’s west, where 34 primary‑school participants took the stage under bright lights.

Organisers note that a single incorrect vowel can determine the outcome, underscoring the intense pressure faced by the young spellers as they compete for the title.

title: NASA to host first air show, Max Power, on Florida's Space Coast this weekend
content:
NASA is set to host its first-ever air show and aerospace expo, titled Max Power, on Florida’s Space Coast. The two-day event will take place on Saturday, Nov. 7, and Sunday, Nov. 8, at and around NASA’s Kennedy Space Center. While the name Max Power is a reference to a "Simpsons" episode where Homer adopts the alias from a hair dryer, the event itself focuses on significant aerospace developments. Tickets are required for attendance, and the schedule includes a variety of presentations, discussions, and live demonstrations.

The Saturday program features an overview of NASA’s "quiet" supersonic jet, the X-59, scheduled for 11:15 a.m. EST. Following this, Nicky Fox and Lori Glaze, heads of NASA’s Science Mission Directorate and Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate respectively, will discuss the agency’s science and exploration goals. The afternoon will include a Q&A with the four astronauts of the Artemis III mission, a session on astronaut preparation for lunar living led by Suzanne Bell of the Behavioral Health and Performance Laboratory, and a discussion on the planned lunar outpost with Moon Base program head Carlos García-Galán. The day concludes with a summary of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope mission by senior project scientist Julie McEnery.

Sunday’s schedule includes a presentation on how NASA uses aircraft for research and an update on the U.S. Space Academy by NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson. Concurrently, astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway from SpaceX’s Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station will participate in a Q&A session. Other highlights include a discussion of the SR-1 Freedom, a planned nuclear-powered spacecraft intended to launch mini-helicopters to Mars in 2028, and a session on X-Planes. The day also features a conversation with an unnamed NASA astronaut and a segment titled "In the Cockpit: Meet the NASA Pilots!"

In addition to the scheduled talks, NASA will hold a livestreamed press conference on Saturday at 5 p.m. EST regarding its moon base plans. This conference will feature Fox, García-Galán, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, and Dayna Ise, the acting director of the Utility and Infrastructure Office for the Moon Base Program. The event will also include dramatic flyovers on both days, some performed by Isaacman, who is described as an accomplished pilot and private astronaut. Isaacman previously funded and commanded the SpaceX Inspiration4 and Polaris Dawn missions, which flew to Earth orbit in September 2021 and September 2024, respectively.

According to the schedule, Isaacman will perform flyovers on both Saturday and Sunday at 11:58 a.m. in an F-5 jet and at 1:31 p.m. in a MiG-29. The event grounds will showcase the newest aircraft, autonomous vehicles, and technologies defining the future of air and space. NASA will display its quiet supersonic X-59 plane, while agency partners will exhibit moon rovers, spacecraft, and other equipment.
summary: NASA will host a first-of-its-kind air show and aerospace expo on Florida's Space Coast this weekend. The show, called Max Power, will take place Saturday and Sunday (Nov.

title: Midnight musical by Todrick Hall criticized for ignoring slavery-era realities
content:
Todrick Hall’s off-Broadway musical, Midnight, centers on a doomed interracial romance set during the era of US slavery in the 1860s. The production features a diverse cast and strong vocals, leading some audience members to compare it to Hamilton. However, unlike Lin-Manuel Miranda’s work, which was based on Ron Chernow’s 2004 biography of Alexander Hamilton, Hall did not utilize source material for Midnight. Instead, the creator and star of the show developed an original narrative that the review describes as neglecting the social realities of its characters.

The plot follows Rail, an enslaved man played by Hall, who falls in love with Richard, a member of the wealthy planter class. Their relationship develops after Richard rents Rail from his owner, Charlotte. Complicating the romance, Rail is in a relationship with Lily Rose, an enslaved woman, while Richard is engaged to Scarlet, a southern belle seeking to secure her family’s financial future through marriage. The story is characterized as a formulaic tale of star-crossed lovers that updates the trope to explore a queer relationship during the time of enslavement.

Hall, a singer, choreographer, and theatre actor, has previously repurposed classics such as Cinderella and Beauty and the Beast through a queer lens, often incorporating modern cultural references like Beyoncé’s music. In Midnight, however, he creates a fantasy that deviates significantly from historical accuracy. The review concludes that the musical fails to effectively imagine the intimate lives of enslaved people, noting that its premise strays so far from historical reality that it misses its intended mark entirely.
summary: Todrick Hall's off-Broadway musical Midnight depicts a doomed interracial romance between an enslaved man and a wealthy planter during the 1860s. Critics argue the show neglects the social realities of its characters by creating a fantasy that deviates from historical accuracy.

title: Wynonna Judd releases raw new album addressing mother's death and personal struggles
content: The country star has abandoned Nashville slickness for a set of raw, pared-back songs that reckon with the death of her mother and decades of personal struggles. ‘This is a labour of love,’ she says When Wynonna Judd appears on my laptop screen – hair a deep shade of crimson, makeup perfect and sporting a huge black baseball cap with Kentucky Queen spelt out across its brim – she looks both fabulous and confident. Which is a good thing, as the Nashville star has been off the radar for a decade. On the occasions her name has made the news, it’s more often been linked to family tragedy than music. “I’m in a good place,” says the woman Rolling Stone described as “the greatest female country singer since Patsy Cline”. “My life has been chaotic. I’ve had a lot of success and a lot of failure, and it’s music that keeps me going. Always.”
summary: Wynonna Judd has abandoned her polished Nashville style for a new album of raw songs that confront the death of her mother and decades of personal struggles. The country star describes the record as a labor of love that reflects her chaotic life and history of success and failure.

title: Florence Pugh Calls Dune Her Generation's Star Wars Ahead of Part Three
content: According to Florence Pugh, Denis Villeneuve’s stunningly strange and breathtaking universe is the equivalent to George Lucas’ heroic space opera. Let’s hope not A long time ago, far far away, in a galaxy called the 1970s, kids dreamed of joining the rebellion, rescuing a princess and blowing up the Death Star. Peer into the cosmic tea leaves and it would become immediately clear that no amount of evildoing could withstand a neurotic gold butler, a dustbin with ideas above its station and a walking seven-foot tall shagpile carpet with a very low tolerance for disagreement. It is worth remembering this when considering Florence Pugh’s recent declaration, ahead of next month’s Dune: Part Three, that Dune is her generation’s Star Wars. And then wondering how much trouble we might be in if she’s actually right. “I think they brought back movie-going. What an event the second [Dune] was,” Pugh cheerfully told the New York Times. “It was just so lovely to be a part of something that we know is our generational kind of Star Wars.”
summary: Florence Pugh stated that Denis Villeneuve's Dune franchise is equivalent to George Lucas' Star Wars. She made this declaration ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, noting that the second film brought audiences back to theaters.

title: The Cat in the Hat review – Bill Hader brings plenty but this animated rework is a mess
content: The SNL alum has an appealing energy and this is an improvement on the 2003 travesty but it’s also far too long and strangely corporate Over a long enough timeline, perhaps every living alumnus of Saturday Night Live will play the Cat in the Hat. Mike Myers kicked off this unexpected tradition by embodying the furry, anarchic Dr Seuss character for a notoriously, almost defiantly ghastly 2003 live-action treatment. After doing us all the service of killing flesh-and-blood Seuss movies for good, Myers was later followed by a more charming Martin Short (via voiceover on a cute PBS/CBC animated series) and now Bill Hader, stepping into the role for a big-budget animated reboot from the oft-flailing animation division of Warner Bros. Just to be clear, this is the same studio that passed on releasing not one but two well-liked features starring their trademark Looney Tunes characters in the last few years. (Puzzlingly, a new Looney Tunes short starring Daffy Duck nonetheless debuts in front of this movie.) Warner has one of the most storied animation libraries in American cinema (and, for that matter, plenty of great animated TV shows like Batman: The Animated Series and Animaniacs) but as far as features go, they’ve never settled on a clear creative vision. They seem just as adrift in a landscape crowded with serious competitors as they were back when everyone was imitating Disney.
summary: The Cat in the Hat review – Bill Hader brings plenty but this animated rework is a mess.

title: FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
content: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League, a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions.
summary: The FA Cup first round proper features 31 ties scheduled to kick off on Saturday at 3pm GMT. The competition stage marks the entry of the bottom two Football League divisions, with focus on non-league clubs.

title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg emerges as NBA’s most entertaining rookie
content:
Yaxel Lendeborg has quickly become one of the most talked‑about newcomers in the NBA. The 24‑year‑old Puerto Rican forward joined the Golden State Warriors and, in his first weeks, has been noted for antagonizing superstars, speaking his mind in the press, and drawing attention away from his teammates.

Lendeborg’s path to the league was unconventional. He spent 12 to 14 hours a day gaming and did not join his high‑school basketball team until he was an upperclassman. He also admitted that he did not really watch the NBA before entering the league. Despite this, he earned enough accolades in college to qualify for the NBA, most notably leading Michigan to its first national championship in 37 years.

The Warriors, still balancing the legacy of their 2010s dynasty with a new core, produced flashes of old greatness to win a single play‑in game before falling in the next. With veteran guard Stephen Curry still at a high level at 38, Lendeborg is seen as a key hope for the team’s future success.

In addition to his on‑court contributions, Lendeborg’s candid takes and willingness to engage with media have made him the season’s most compelling personality, a role he embraces even though he reportedly first heard the term “media training” only in college.
summary: Yaxel Lendeborg, a 24‑year‑old Puerto Rican forward for the Golden State Warriors, has spent his first weeks in the NBA antagonizing superstars and drawing media attention. He previously led Michigan to its first national championship in 37 years after not debuting on his high school basketball team until his upperclassman years.

title: Lebanon, Ukraine, and Syria Rugby Teams Compete Despite Home Wars
content:
Rugby league players from Lebanon, Syria, and Ukraine have continued to compete internationally despite ongoing conflicts in their home countries. In Sydney, Syria played a series of friendlies at the Bankstown Bulls' home ground, while Lebanon faced France in a World Cup match at CommBank Stadium. Additionally, Ukraine participated in a European Championship fixture in Belgrade. The Lebanon team secured a victory over France following a dramatic finish, a result that suggests they remain among the top eight teams globally, although their official ranking is lower due to inactivity since the last World Cup.

Prop Jalal Bazzaz, who played in all three of Lebanon’s World Cup matches, noted that the team's last gathering was in England in 2022. He stated that the players aimed to perform well each week and give back to their roots. Bazzaz described representing his country as putting Lebanon on the world stage, providing people with something to smile about and offering a sense of hope. The athletes from these war-torn nations expressed determination to give people hope, put their countries on the map, and wear their national badges with honor.
summary: Players from Lebanon, Syria, and Ukraine stated they compete to give their people hope and put their countries on the map despite ongoing wars at home. Lebanon recently defeated France in a World Cup match, while Syria and Ukraine played international fixtures in Sydney and Belgrade.
