title: Amanda McKinney projected to win Washington's 4th Congressional District
content:
Amanda McKinney, a Yakima County commissioner, is projected to win Washington’s 4th Congressional District, according to Decision Desk HQ.  

She defeated Air Force veteran John Duresky (D) in the race for the seat, which covers a large portion of the eastern half of the Evergreen State, an area that is more rural.
summary: Amanda McKinney projected to win Washington's 4th Congressional District.
author: The Hill

title: Meta, TikTok, Google sue California over child online safety law
content: Meta, TikTok, and Google have filed separate lawsuits against California, arguing that the state’s new “Digital Age Assurance Act” violates their First Amendment rights. The bipartisan legislation, which takes effect on January 1, prohibits social media platforms in the state from providing addictive services to children.
summary: Meta, TikTok, and Google filed separate lawsuits against California, arguing that the new legislation violates their First Amendment rights. The state's "Digital Age Assurance Act," which takes effect on January 1, bans social media platforms from providing addictive services to children.
author: The Hill

title: Top Democrat vows ‘vigorous’ oversight of Pentagon
content: Rep. Adam Smith (D-Wash.), the ranking member of the House Armed Services Committee, pledged on Wednesday to conduct “vigorous” oversight of the Pentagon. Smith stated that this effort would include seeking testimonies from senior officials.
summary: Top Democrat vows ‘vigorous’ oversight of Pentagon.
author: The Hill

title: Democrat Jessica Killin flips longtime GOP-held Colorado House seat
content: Democrat Jessica Killin is projected to unseat Representative Jeff Crank in Colorado’s 5th Congressional District, according to Decision Desk HQ. This victory marks a political first for the Colorado Springs-area district, which has never elected a Democrat since its creation in 1973. Killin is an Army veteran who previously served as chief of staff.
summary: Democrat Jessica Killin flips longtime GOP-held Colorado House seat.
author: The Hill

title: Washington voters approve ban on transgender girls in school sports
content: Washington voters are projected to approve a ballot measure reversing the state’s long-standing policy allowing transgender girls to compete on girls’ and women’s school sports teams, according to Decision Desk HQ. The new measure requires students to submit healthcare provider documentation verifying their sex before participating on girls’ teams.
summary: Washington voters are projected to reverse a state policy allowing transgender girls to compete on girls’ school sports teams. The measure requires students to submit healthcare provider documentation verifying their sex before playing on a girls’ team.
author: The Hill

title: Newsom announces he will commute sentences of inmates on California's death row
content: California Governor Gavin Newsom announced that he is commuting the sentences of all inmates on the state's Death Row. The governor stated that the facility currently holds 548 people, which he described as the largest death row in the Western Hemisphere.
summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced that he's commuting the sentences of all inmates on the state's Death Row.
author: NPR Politics

title: VR headsets lower presurgery anxiety and distress in children
content: A study by Dayanjan Wijesinghe of Virginia Commonwealth University, published in PLOS Digital Health, found that children using virtual reality headsets before surgery experienced reduced self-reported distress and fear. The research also noted lower heart rates and blood pressure in these patients.
summary: A study found that children using virtual reality before surgery reported less distress and fear. The participants also exhibited lower heart rates and blood pressure compared to those who did not use the technology.
author: Medical Xpress

title: COVID-19-related stress linked to faster epigenetic aging in adolescents
content: Researchers have linked COVID-19-related stress to faster epigenetic aging in adolescents, revealing biological consequences of the pandemic that had not previously been explored. While the pandemic and associated measures caused significant stress affecting physical and mental health across society, this study specifically identified impacts at the epigenetic level among young people. The findings have been published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic and its associated measures caused significant stress across all levels of society, negatively impacting physical and mental health. The biological consequences of this stress have not yet been explored.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study links indoor radon to higher heart failure risk in postmenopausal women
content: New research published in JAMA Network Open indicates that postmenopausal women residing in areas with higher estimated indoor radon levels may face an increased risk of heart failure. The study, led by researchers at the UNC Gillings School of Global Public Health, provides the latest evidence suggesting that radon exposure could present a significant threat to the cardiac health of aging women.
summary: The study of postmenopausal women found that those living in areas with higher estimated indoor radon levels may have a higher risk of heart failure. The research was published in JAMA Network Open and was led by researchers at the UNC Gillings School of Global Public Health.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Karolinska Institutet and Mayo Clinic researchers publish review on early celiac disease stages
content:
As research into the interplay between genetics and environmental risk factors in early celiac disease expands, the need to harmonize scientific terms and concepts in the field has grown. In response, an effort led by researchers at Karolinska Institutet and the Mayo Clinic has brought together 22 scientists from seven countries to address this challenge.

The collaborative team has published a review detailing the stages of early celiac disease. This paper, which aims to standardize terminology and concepts, has been published in the journal Gut.
summary: Researchers at Karolinska Institutet and the Mayo Clinic led a group of 22 scientists from seven countries to publish a review on the stages of early celiac disease. The paper, addressing the need to harmonize scientific terms and concepts, appears in the journal Gut.
author: Medical Xpress

title: I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed
content: The article explores how negative job interview experiences can offer valuable insights into the professional world. It highlights that while these encounters are often unpleasant, they serve as learning opportunities for navigating the job market.
summary: I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed.
author: BBC Business

title: Employers Tighten Hybrid Rules as Employees Shift to Home Work
content: Office attendance from Monday to Friday was once a standard requirement for many jobs, but employees have increasingly developed a preference for working from home. In response to this shift, some employers have begun tightening their rules regarding hybrid work arrangements.
summary: Office attendance from Monday to Friday used to be a standard requirement for many jobs. Employees now prefer working from home, prompting some employers to tighten hybrid work rules.
author: Phys.org

title: Study links opaque Italian soccer club ownership to higher financial and criminal risks
content: The provided text poses questions regarding the ultimate ownership of Italian soccer clubs and the origins of their investment funds. It highlights the challenges in identifying individual controllers due to the use of investment funds, fiduciary companies, and transnational corporate structures. The content suggests that these opaque ownership arrangements are associated with higher financial and criminal risks.
summary: The article examines the difficulty in identifying ultimate owners of Italian soccer clubs due to complex structures like investment funds and transnational corporations. It highlights that such opaque ownership is associated with increased financial and criminal risks.

title: Wageningen research shows fish migration needs maintenance beyond fish passes
content:
The Netherlands is constructing fish passes to restore accessibility for fish in rivers and streams.

content:

title: Airbnb to launch AI travel agent by first half of 2027
content:
Airbnb announced in its Q3 2026 earnings shareholder letter that it will launch an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027. The new agent is intended to help users plan and book trips through the platform.

The company noted that while current AI agents excel at routine tasks such as restaurant reservations or appointment scheduling, planning a trip on Airbnb involves additional complexity. Airbnb says its strengths—matching hosts and guests, its established role in reservations, and a new interface built specifically for travel—provide a competitive edge for the upcoming AI agent.

title: OpenAI to Stop Using NDAs with Public Officials on Data Center Projects
content:
OpenAI announced it will step back from using non‑disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials on its data‑center projects. The move follows a week of midterm elections in which voters strongly opposed data‑center expansion.

The company said it will now allow only narrow protections that cover legitimate security information, trade secrets, or other competitively sensitive data. This change comes after scrutiny of previous projects that relied on NDAs to conceal discussions between developers and local officials.
summary: OpenAI announced it will no longer use non‑disclosure agreements with public officials for its data center projects. The company will instead provide only narrow protections for legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.

title: Democrats Flip Five State Governorships, Clearing Path for Clean Energy
content:
Democrats gained significant state‑level control after Tuesday’s elections. Prior to the vote, Republicans had more governorships, state legislative seats, and a majority of state trifectas—governor plus both legislative chambers. Those advantages have now vanished, according to analysts and advocates, opening the door for new climate and clean‑energy legislation.

The Democratic sweep of competitive races flipped the governorships in Georgia, Iowa, Ohio, Nevada, and Texas from Republican to Democratic hands. This shift is expected to empower the party to advance its clean‑energy agenda at the state level.
summary: Democrats swept the majority of competitive state races, flipping governorships in Georgia, Iowa, Ohio, Nevada, and Texas. The loss of Republican advantage in governorships and state legislative seats opens the way for more climate and clean energy legislation.

title: NASA unveils mysterious X-70 experimental aircraft using AI-generated image
content:
NASA announced the X‑70 Fractal, an experimental aircraft that will feature reconfigurable flight‑control technology and a modular design allowing different payloads to be swapped in and out.  The agency said much remains unknown about the aircraft’s design and development timeline, although NASA administrator Jared Isaacman indicated the X‑plane could take flight within two years.

The announcement highlighted a mystery surrounding the new X‑plane.  NASA’s press release included an apparently AI‑generated image of the X‑70, showing a dark silhouette vaguely resembling a military fighter jet obscured by smoke.  Isaacman explained that the image was part of the agency’s effort to illustrate the aircraft’s potential appearance.

Isaacman made the announcement during the UP. Summit held at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida on November 4.  He said, “The X‑70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high‑performance platform to test advanced flight‑control, maneuverability, and other cutting‑edge technologies in real flight,” adding that its modular design and rapid payload swapping will keep teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next.
summary: NASA has announced a new experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, that will supposedly feature reconfigurable flight-control technology and a modular design for swapping in different payloads. But much remains unknown about the aircraft’s design and development timeline, even as NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said the X-plane could take flight within two years.

title: Vulnerability *sshole Lets Hackers SSH into Alpine Linux Devices Without Password
content:
Alpine Linux users are warned that a decade‑old flaw in the way OpenSSH interacts with the musl C library can let attackers gain password‑less SSH access to affected devices. The vulnerability appears only when OpenSSH is built against musl and the system does not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules). Alpine, a lightweight distribution that relies on musl, is the most widely known platform that can be impacted, though other distributions with similar configurations may also be at risk.

For an attacker to succeed, two additional conditions must be met. First, the target system must have at least one user account whose password hash uses SHA256 or SHA512. Second, the account targeted by the exploit must be configured as passwordless, indicated by a “*” in the password field of /etc/shadow. Passwordless accounts are typically used for certificate‑based authentication, a common setup for certain user types.
summary: Vulnerability *sshole Lets Hackers SSH into Alpine Linux Devices Without Password.

title: On this day in space! Nov. 5, 2002: NASA's Galileo spacecraft flies by Jupiter moon Amalthea only to find it's a 'pile of icy rubble less dense than water'
content:
On November 5, 2002, NASA’s Galileo spacecraft conducted a flyby of the Jupiter moon Amalthea while operating with minimal fuel reserves. This event marked the final time the probe swung by one of Jupiter’s moons. During the encounter, Galileo passed within 99 miles of Amalthea, which also represented the closest approach the spacecraft would make to Jupiter before its eventual descent into the planet’s atmosphere in September 2005. The flyby occurred in a region of strong radiation from Jupiter, which posed significant hazards to the spacecraft.

The proximity to Amalthea triggered technical difficulties for Galileo, causing the spacecraft to enter safe mode just 30 minutes after passing the moon. NASA officials indicated they were prepared for such issues given the spacecraft’s deteriorating condition and the intense radiation environment. The problem was quickly resolved, allowing Galileo to resume operations. The mission concluded less than a year later when the spacecraft intentionally crashed into Jupiter’s atmosphere on September 21, 2005, where it was crushed by high pressure.

Scientific analysis of the data collected during the flyby revealed that Amalthea is a pile of icy rubble with a density lower than water. NASA announced these findings in May 2005. Torrence Johnson, a study co-author and project scientist for the Galileo mission at JPL, noted that the moon’s density is well below that of water ice. He stated that despite substantial porosity, Amalthea likely contains a significant amount of water ice as well as rock.

Amalthea is distinguished as the reddest object in the solar system, a characteristic attributed to sulfur contamination on its surface. Although Galileo’s images of the moon appear in black and white, the red tint is a known feature. The moon measures approximately 168 miles in length and orbits Jupiter at a distance of about 112,468 miles, significantly closer to the planet than the Earth is to its own moon. Scientists also noted that Amalthea generates more heat than it receives from the sun, potentially due to electrical currents created as it moves through Jupiter’s magnetic field.

Originally designated Jupiter V, Amalthea was the fifth Jupiter moon discovered after the Galilean moons: Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto. It was named after a water nymph from Greek mythology. The moon holds the distinction of being the last Jupiter moon discovered through visual observations, having been first identified by astronomer Edward Emerson Barnard in September 1892 using the Lick Observatory telescope in California.
summary: On Nov. 5, 2002, NASA's old Galileo spacecraft was almost out of fuel.

title: I Play Rocky review – Anthony Ippolito adds knockout sweetness to the story of Stallone’s Hollywood triumph
content:
The review praises the film I Play Rocky for capturing the humor, passion, and grit of Sylvester Stallone’s journey from minor roles to Oscar glory. Described as a mythic making-of tale, the drama details how the struggling Italian-American actor, who had previously worked in softcore pornography, wrote a screenplay inspired by boxer Chuck Wepner. Wepner’s brief knockout of Muhammad Ali in 1975 served as the inspiration for the script.

Stallone’s tremendous self-belief is highlighted as he insisted on playing the lead role in his own 1976 boxing movie. He held out against substantial cash offers that would have allowed him to keep the writing credit while casting an established star. The review characterizes the film as a very enjoyable drama about duplicates and surfaces, noting that while it may not be profound, it delivers the transcendental thrill of success.
summary: I Play Rocky review – Anthony Ippolito adds knockout sweetness to the story of Stallone’s Hollywood triumph.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Jan Potocki's The Manuscript Found in Saragossa Featured in New Exhibition
content:
Jan Potocki’s The Manuscript Found in Saragossa is described as one of the least-known great novels of the European canon, featuring a surreal and mysterious plot. The story follows Alphonse van Worden, a young Walloon officer traveling through the Sierra Morena to join the Spanish army. During his journey, he experiences an erotic encounter with two demonic Moorish sisters, encounters shape-shifting apparitions, and is tested by a Jewish Kabbalist who attempts to use mystical formulas to control spirits and decipher the universe.

The novel, an encyclopedic roman-monde written more than 200 years ago, has amassed a cult following that includes Salman Rushdie and Jerry Garcia. Curators of a new exhibition argue that the book’s global humanism makes it relevant today. The provided text also poses the question of whether the author, Jan Potocki, believed he was a werewolf, highlighting the outlandish origin story associated with the work.
summary: A new exhibition highlights Jan Potocki's 200-year-old novel, The Manuscript Found in Saragossa, which has a cult following that includes Salman Rushdie and Jerry Garcia. The book follows a young officer through surreal encounters in the Sierra Morena and is described by curators as having global humanism.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Russell Brand faces significant prison term after rape and sexual assault convictions
content:
Russell Brand, a 51-year-old actor and comedian, has been found guilty of raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others. The conviction concludes a lengthy legal process that has drawn attention to how Brand committed these offenses while at the peak of his fame. During his trial, prosecutors characterized him as a ruthless, calculated, and manipulative sexual predator.

The specific charges include the rape of a woman at his luxury London townhouse. Additionally, Brand was convicted of sexually assaulting women in front of his entourage at various locations, including their workplaces, a radio station, and a TV studio. The verdict marks a significant turning point in the years-long legal saga surrounding the entertainer.
summary: Russell Brand was found guilty of raping a woman and sexually assaulting three other women. He was convicted for crimes committed at his London townhouse and various workplaces.

title: Jimmy Anderson in contract talks with Surrey after Lancashire exit
content:
Jimmy Anderson has opened talks with Division One side Surrey regarding a contract for next season, following his release by Lancashire last month after 25 years at Old Trafford. The 44-year-old, identified as England’s leading wicket-taker, has received numerous expressions of interest since his departure, with Surrey reportedly making a firm move by offering him a deal.

The club is growing in confidence that Anderson will accept the offer, which would mark a remarkable swansong for the seamer. Meanwhile, Nottinghamshire is also monitoring the situation as the former Lancashire player considers his next steps in county cricket.
summary: Jimmy Anderson has opened talks with Surrey to sign a contract for next season following his release by Lancashire. The Division One side is confident the 44-year-old will join them, while Nottinghamshire is also monitoring the situation.

title: Wallabies pay dispute with Rugby Australia overshadows Nations Championship finale
content: Australia are preparing for their clash with England under a cloud with RA claiming the players’ union’s proposals ‘threaten the future of the game’ An increasingly ugly pay dispute is threatening to unravel Australian rugby a year from a home World Cup, as the Wallabies prepare for four Nations Championship matches crucial for reversing fortunes smashed by two heavy Bledisloe Cup defeats. The Wallabies meet England at Allianz Stadium – the sponsor’s name for Twickenham, not its namesake in Sydney – on Sunday afternoon local time (early Monday AEDT). The fixture is critical as the team looks to revive the momentum developed early under new coach Les Kiss before Australia were given a reality check against New Zealand last month.
summary: Australia is preparing for a match against England while facing a pay dispute where Rugby Australia claims player union proposals threaten the future of the game. The fixture is critical for the Wallabies to reverse momentum lost after two heavy Bledisloe Cup defeats.

title: Spain manager Luis de la Fuente attends funeral of Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel
content:
Jesús de Miguel Alameda, a striker for Tenerife, was laid to rest in his family’s village of Navahermosa after dying from an on-field collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days prior. The funeral cortege traveled from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel in a silence that filled the narrow streets, which were crowded with mourners despite the village’s small population of 3,587.

Spain manager Luis de la Fuente attended the service, stating that the football community comes together more than ever in moments of pain. He expressed a desire to be close to De Miguel’s parents, wife, and daughter, noting that there were few words to offer during such a difficult time.

Tenerife president Felipe Miñambres emphasized the need for professional help to get through the tragedy. The club’s majority shareholder, Rayco García, who had wept while leaving the location where De Miguel’s body lay in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, pledged to his teammates that they would forever take care of De Miguel’s daughter, Clara.
summary: The funeral for Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel was held in his family's village of Navahermosa, attended by Spain manager Luis de la Fuente. De Miguel died three days earlier after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lewis Hamilton refuses to back down over criticism of Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc
content:
Lewis Hamilton has refused to back down over his criticism of Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc following a clash at last weekend’s Mexico Grand Prix. During the race’s opening lap, Leclerc attempted to pass Hamilton at turn four but went off track. This incident left Hamilton vulnerable, allowing Max Verstappen to overtake him and ultimately win the race, which cost Ferrari a potential one-two finish.

Hamilton stated that he has worked hard to build a relationship with Leclerc. Despite the on-track conflict, the driver maintains his position regarding the criticism leveled at his teammate after the incident in Mexico.
summary: Lewis Hamilton refused to back down after criticizing his Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc following a clash at the Mexico Grand Prix. The incident occurred when Leclerc went off track attempting to pass Hamilton, which left Hamilton vulnerable to Max Verstappen.

title: Study: COVID-19 vaccines yielded up to $64.3 trillion in first-year benefits
content:
A reanalysis of data regarding the economic impact of coronavirus vaccines suggests that the health and economic benefits provided in the first year of rollout were worth up to $64.3 trillion, nearly double previous estimates. Earlier calculations indicated that the $79.4 billion invested in developing these vaccines yielded a global return between $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion in the first 12 months. The updated figures now place the return between $6.43 trillion and $64.3 trillion, meaning that for every dollar spent on vaccine development, between $59.70 and $809 was gained during that period.

The disparity in the upper estimate stems from the analytical methods employed. The lower figure of $6.43 trillion is derived from a cost-effectiveness analysis commonly used in the health sector, which incorporates quality of life factors. In contrast, the higher figure of $64.3 trillion is based on a cost-benefit analysis typical of the public sector. Both analyses utilized data from 173 countries, accounting for averted hospitalizations, productivity losses, and lives saved. One specific model used by the researchers suggested that the vaccines prevented between 14 million and 20 million deaths in their first year.

Hallie Benjamin of the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine stated that the publication demonstrates the substantial health and financial benefits of the vaccines relative to their development and delivery costs. The initial, lower estimates were released when the research was in a preprint stage, prior to peer review. Benjamin noted that numerous changes made during the peer-review process strengthened the quality of the findings. A key methodological adjustment involved shifting from the Value of Statistical Life Years to the Value of Statistical Life. Mark Jit of New York University explained that this change treats life spans more equally and aligns with recommendations for valuing mortality-risk reductions. Additionally, the cost-benefit analysis figure increased significantly due to a modification in how the economic value of avoiding a death was calculated.

Despite the overall high returns, the benefits were not evenly distributed globally. The researchers found that richer countries experienced the highest returns, likely because poorer nations accessed the vaccines later. This delay resulted in fewer lives saved and reduced averted productivity and healthcare costs in those regions. Jit described these results as a message highlighting the need for fair vaccine distribution to those most in need worldwide.

Richard Carpiano of the University of California, Riverside, noted that while the vaccines were already recognized as a life-saving success, this study reinforces the principle that protecting public health also protects the economy. He argued that this challenges previous "black-and-white" thinking regarding the trade-off between public health measures, such as lockdowns, and economic protection. Carpiano expressed hope that these insights will inform policy-making for future infectious disease outbreaks and pandemics, noting that the probability of another pandemic in the next decade is significant. The study was published in PLOS Medicine.
summary: Study: COVID-19 vaccines yielded up to $64.3 trillion in first-year benefits.

title: Gamers use capture cards and Veyra to apply DLSS 5 to GTA VI console footage
content:
Gamers are preparing to apply Nvidia’s DLSS 5 technology to the console-exclusive Grand Theft Auto VI, despite the game not being available on PC this month. On an unmoderated GTAVI subreddit, user RevolutionaryBus8208 proposed a setup that routes a PlayStation 5 through a 4K capture card to a PC. The video signal then passes through Veyra, an open-source tool capable of applying DLSS 5’s AI-powered neural rendering to video content. This process also utilizes DLSS frame generation to increase the 30 fps source to a 90 fps output before piping the signal back to a 4K TV.

To demonstrate this potential, RevolutionaryBus8208 used Veyra to upscale the Grand Theft Auto VI Extended Look trailer from August. The modified version exhibits sharper background elements, subtler shadows, and more believable light scattering on certain surfaces compared to the original. However, the demonstration also reveals drawbacks, including a washed-out appearance with less deep blacks and an unnaturally smooth soap opera effect in some scenes.

title: Kalshi loses appeals courts on state gambling law challenges
content:
Kalshi has faced a series of legal setbacks this week as two federal circuit appeals courts rejected its efforts to block state gambling laws in Connecticut, New York, and Nevada. The prediction market company is also confronting a new lawsuit filed by the Arkansas attorney general. In these disputes, the central question is whether state gambling regulations apply to prediction markets, a stance Kalshi disputes by arguing that its platform offers "swaps" subject only to regulation by the US Commodity Futures Exchange (CFTC).

Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin announced the lawsuit by stating that while Kalshi insists its products are not gambling, Arkansas law focuses on substance rather than semantics. Griffin noted that Kalshi allows customers to wager money on the outcome of nearly anything, which he described as prohibited under state law for unregulated platforms. The Trump administration is reportedly aligned with Kalshi in these legal battles, with Donald Trump Jr. serving as an advisor to the company in exchange for an equity deal.
summary: Two circuit appeals courts rejected Kalshi's attempts to block state gambling laws in Connecticut, New York, and Nevada. Kalshi also faces a new lawsuit from Arkansas attorney general Tim Griffin, who argues that its prediction market violates Arkansas law.

title: New Software Improves Webb Telescope Exoplanet Imaging
content:
Researchers have developed a new software package designed to enhance the James Webb Space Telescope’s ability to image exoplanets. The primary challenge in direct imaging and atmospheric analysis is the overwhelming brightness of host stars compared to the faint light from their planets. Although coronagraphs can block much of this stellar light, their effectiveness is limited by noise resulting from subtle variations in the telescope’s configuration and pointing between observations. The new software optimizes a physical model of the telescope to better account for these differences, enabling the production of low-noise images.

The development relies on the concept of the point spread function, which describes how a telescope distorts a point of light. Due to hardware imperfections and pointing limitations, a single point of light does not appear as a sharp dot but rather as a slightly blurry, spread-out shape. By refining the mathematical description of this distortion, the software allows researchers to more accurately model these variations. This approach aims to support the next steps in exoplanet research, specifically efforts to infer surface conditions or capture light that has passed through planetary atmospheres.
summary: Researchers developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the Webb Telescope to better model differences caused by noise, producing low‑noise imaging of exoplanets. The software improves the telescope's point spread function modeling, helping to image exoplanets directly.

title: BMW 2027 i7 60 xDrive review: Neue Klasse powertrain and cylindrical cells
content:
BMW has updated its electric vehicle lineup by transitioning from prismatic battery cells to more energy-dense cylindrical cell arrangements. The new drive units feature silicon carbide inverters and more compact packaging, while retaining electrically excited synchronous motors. This sixth-generation electric powertrain was originally designed for the Neue Klasse family, which replaces numerous discrete electronic control units with a smaller number of powerful domain controllers. These new computers offer faster processing power, enhancing capabilities in chassis control and powertrain efficiency, and allow for easier software updates.

The 2027 i7 60 xDrive represents the latest iteration of BMW’s strategy for large luxury sedans, where the electric powertrain is offered as a direct option alongside internal combustion engines rather than as a separate model line. Ars Technica recently drove the 2027 i7, as well as the 2027 iX5 and X5, during a media event. For this trip, BMW provided flights from Washington, DC, to Los Angeles and accommodation. Ars Technica notes that it does not accept paid editorial content.
summary: BMW provided Ars Technica with the 2027 i7 60 xDrive for a test drive from Washington, DC, to Los Angeles. The vehicle utilizes the sixth-generation electric powertrain designed for the Neue Klasse family, featuring cylindrical cells and silicon carbide inverters.

title: NC woman indicted after using ChatGPT to plan husband's murder
content: ChatGPT allegedly helped a North Carolina woman, Cheryl Gates, craft a “personalized plan” to poison her husband, James, after fueling her delusions that he planned to divorce her and leave her with nothing. A grand jury indicted Cheryl Gates on charges of attempted first-degree murder and food contamination in October. About a week prior, the accusations that ChatGPT was a co-conspirator in the attempted murder came in a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court that was made public this week. In it, James Gates alleged that OpenAI and Sam Altman failed to employ technical safeguards to shut down Cheryl’s chats even after her queries became “obviously suspicious” and sought advice on how to execute and conceal a homicide. At first, Cheryl told ChatGPT that she was researching poisoning out of fear that her husband might possibly try to kill her—framing her queries as “self-protection.” Coming to the rescue, ChatGPT did not terminate the conversation. Instead, it helped her “with specific instructions for the preparation, dosage, and administration of Oleander, including whether anti-nausea medicine would accelerate or inhibit death, whether it would show on an autopsy report, and whether it could be injected into a vein or muscle instead of being ingested in tea and have the same lethal effect,” the lawsuit said. title: Google says schools can keep search but must opt‑in to AI products
content:
Google has clarified its new AI policy for K–12 schools following backlash from educators and parents over earlier reports. The company stated that its updated approach is designed to provide schools with greater control over AI usage. Under the new guidelines, schools utilizing Google applications must opt into specific AI products, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Gemini in Classroom.

Contrary to initial interpretations that suggested Google would block search access for schools rejecting AI, the company explained that it technically offers more choice than previous arrangements. While Google classifies search as part of its AI portfolio, it will not automatically disable the feature. Instead, schools will retain the authority to decide whether to enable search for logged-in student accounts, allowing them to align their settings with internal AI policies. This clarification aims to address concerns that the policy was perceived as coercive, emphasizing that the decision to turn on or off specific AI tools rests with the educational institution.
summary: Google announced a new AI policy for K‑12 schools that requires schools using Google apps to opt into its AI products, including search. The company clarified that search will not be automatically disabled if schools reject AI, giving schools the choice to keep search while skipping Gemini.

summary: Meta's AI agent can now take calls as a customizable animated avatar. This feature comes ahead of the launch of a Tamagotchi-like wearable designed to bring Muse to life.
author: TechCrunch

title: Serve Robotics Launches Physical AI Services Business Line
content: Serve Robotics, in its third‑quarter earnings release, announced a new business line called Physical AI Services. The new unit will provide customers with connectivity and data tools.
summary: Serve Robotics announced it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services. The line will offer customers its connectivity and data tools.
author: TechCrunch

title: Elon Musk's $446M PAC Spend Fails as Democrats Win All 5 Senate Races
content:
The tech sector invested heavily in the U.S. midterm elections, but the return on that spending was disappointing. Elon Musk contributed a total of $446 million to Republican‑aligned political action committees and affiliated groups since last year, yet the money did not translate into electoral gains. In every one of the five Senate contests where Musk’s America Pac spent the most backing Republican candidates, the Democrats emerged victorious.

The Guardian’s U.S. tech editor, Blake Montgomery, joined hosts Carter Sherman and Kai Wright to discuss the broader fallout. They explored what the so‑called “blue tsunami” could mean for Musk, the wider technology industry, and whether it might signal a shift in the future of AI data centers. The conversation also touched on potential implications for the U.S. economy.
summary: Elon Musk's $446M PAC Spend Fails as Democrats Win All 5 Senate Races.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Nasdaq Falls Nearly $2 Trillion on AI Regulation Concerns After Election
content: Nearly $2tn shaved off Nasdaq value as worries of curbs to AI datacenters ripple across bourses The Nasdaq share index had its worst day in 18 months after slumping 5.5% on Thursday amid growing signs that the artificial intelligence industry will face tougher regulation because of the midterm election results. As Wall Street sustained widespread losses, the Nasdaq composite tumbled into “correction territory” – more than 10% below its recent record high – with more than $2tn shaved off its value by the end of trading Thursday. The tech-heavy index had its biggest one-day fall since Donald Trump announced his “liberation day” tariffs on US trading partners in April 2025.
summary: The Nasdaq composite dropped 5.5% on Thursday, its worst day in 18 months. The decline erased more than $2 trillion in market value amid concerns that AI datacenters may face stricter regulation following the midterm election.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Drone strike ignites Ozon warehouse in Adygeysk, southern Russia
content: A fire erupted at an Ozon warehouse in Adygeysk, southern Russia, on Wednesday. The Russian e‑commerce giant confirmed the facility was targeted in a drone attack.
summary: A fire broke out at an Ozon warehouse in Adygeysk, southern Russia, on Wednesday. The Russian e-commerce giant said the facility was targeted in a drone attack.

title: Tehran demonstrators burn banner of US and Israeli leaders at 1979 embassy takeover rally
content: Demonstrators in Tehran burned a banner that showed U.S. and Israeli leaders during rallies that marked the 1979 U.S. embassy takeover. The protests occurred after a major electoral setback for Donald Trump.
summary: Demonstrators in Tehran burned a banner depicting US and Israeli leaders during rallies marking the 1979 US embassy takeover. The protests followed a major electoral setback for Donald Trump.

title: North Korea urges EU to stay out of UN human rights resolution
content: The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights said last year that human rights in North Korea have shown no improvement over the past decade and had in fact worsened in many cases.
summary: North Korea told the EU to mind its own business after a draft UN resolution on human rights. The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights said that human rights in North Korea have shown no improvement over the past decade and have worsened in many cases.

title: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña Resigns Amid Ueno Bank Crisis
content:
Santiago Peña resigned as president of Paraguay amid the Ueno Bank crisis and was later impeached over an alleged conflict of interest. Vice President Pedro Alliana will take office.

Millions of Paraguayans—about three million—are waiting to recover their deposits as the bank collapse leaves them without access to their accounts.
summary: Santiago Peña resigned as president of Paraguay amid the Ueno Bank crisis and was later impeached over an alleged conflict of interest. Vice President Pedro Alliana will take office while millions of Paraguayans wait to recover their deposits.

title: Zelensky urges Spain, Latin America to help repair Ukraine's power grid
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has appealed to Spain and Latin American countries for urgent assistance in repairing Ukraine’s damaged energy infrastructure. During the Ibero‑American Summit in Madrid, he also met King Felipe VI.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to Spain and Latin American countries for urgent help repairing Ukraine's damaged energy infrastructure. He also met King Felipe VI during the Ibero‑American Summit in Madrid.

title: Palestinian farmers harvest olives with limited access as Israeli troops fire tear gas
content: Palestinian farmers in the occupied West Bank have been permitted only limited access to their olive groves because of Israeli military restrictions. During the harvest, many discovered damaged trees, and soldiers fired tear‑gas near the workers.
summary: Palestinian farmers in the occupied West Bank were allowed limited access to their olive groves under Israeli military restrictions. Many discovered damaged trees, and soldiers fired tear gas near the harvest.

title: France sees new protests as government moves to prevent violence
content: France is witnessing fresh protests as the government moves to avoid a repeat of the October unrest. Demonstrators are calling for improved public services, notably education, and are voicing concerns over the rising cost of living. The coverage is reported from the scene by FRANCE 24’s Claire Paccalin.
summary: France is facing new protests as the government seeks to avoid a repeat of October unrest. Demonstrators demand better public services, including education, and criticize the rising cost-of-living, FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin reports from the ground.
author: France 24

title: Paraguay's President Peña Impeached Minutes After Resignation Over Banking Scandal
content: Paraguay’s lower house voted unanimously to impeach President Santiago Peña on Thursday, just minutes after he announced his resignation on X. Protesters have rallied in the streets since the takeover of a bank linked to Peña blocked millions of people, including pensioners, from accessing their money.
summary: Paraguay’s lower house unanimously voted to impeach President Santiago Peña on Thursday, minutes after he announced his resignation on X. Protesters have rallied in the streets since the takeover of a bank linked to Peña blocked millions of people, including pensioners, from accessing their money.
author: France 24

title: Solidaires leader Gaëlle Martinez calls for more public services, higher salaries, better schools
content: As France confronts another wave of strikes and protests, Gaëlle Martinez, National Secretary of the trade union Solidaires, presents the general strike as more than a confrontation over wages, public spending or the cost of living. Her account reveals a deeper struggle over economic dignity, the future of public services and the democratic right to collective protest. “People just want to live, not survive.” For Martinez, deteriorating schools, insufficient salaries and the dismantling of public services are not isolated policy failures. They are interconnected symptoms of political and economic priorities that, in her assessment, place fiscal restraint above social welfare. Her demand for “a new budget” that is “not based on cuts” is accompanied by a call to “tax the biggest companies, the richest companies where the profits are made.”
summary: Gaëlle Martinez, National Secretary of the trade union Solidaires, says France’s general strike reflects concerns over deteriorating schools, low salaries and cuts to public services. She demands a new budget without cuts and proposes taxing the biggest and richest companies.
author: France 24

title: Myanmar junta launches September offensive in Rakhine, intensifies civilian airstrikes
content: More than five years after Myanmar’s military coup, the junta began a new offensive in September aimed at retaking Rakhine State. The operation has intensified airstrikes targeting civilians and includes the use of double‑tap strikes, according to the report.
summary: More than five years after the military coup, the junta launched a new offensive in September to retake Rakhine State. The offensive has intensified airstrikes against civilians and includes double‑tap strikes.
author: France 24

title: Gov. Gavin Newsom to commute all 548 California death sentences to life without parole
content: California Governor Gavin Newsom announced on Thursday that he will commute all 548 death sentences in the state to life in prison without parole. The move represents a significant shift away from capital punishment as Newsom prepares to leave office after eight years.
summary: Governor Gavin Newsom said on Thursday he will commute all 548 death sentences in California to life in prison without parole. The move marks a major step away from capital punishment as he prepares to leave office after eight years.
author: France 24

title: French protests broaden to challenge government as Le Pen and Mélenchon become objective allies
content: “You can be as repressive as you want. The grievances are still here.” With this stark observation, Ariane Bogain, lecturer in French and politics at Northumbria University, captures the central dilemma confronting the French government: how can political authority be restored when the social and economic grievances driving public anger remain unresolved? Bogain and French politics editor Marc Perelman join Delano D'Souza to examine a protest movement that has evolved beyond its initial demands over purchasing power, fuel prices and education into a broader challenge to the French government. Perelman identifies a striking political paradox: Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, despite occupying opposing ideological positions, are “objective allies” in their shared electoral interest in weakening the political centre.
summary: Lecturer Ariane Bogain and French politics editor Marc Perelman say the French protests have moved beyond demands on purchasing power, fuel prices and education to a broader challenge to the government. Perelman describes Marine Le Pen and Jean‑Luc Mélenchon as “objective allies” who share an electoral interest in weakening the political centre.
author: France 24

title: Nigerian court disqualifies leading presidential candidate two months before election
content:
A Nigerian court has disqualified a leading presidential candidate, creating fresh complications for the electoral process two months before the scheduled election. The ruling was reported in the evening edition of the news program.

Separately, tens of thousands of people have crossed the border into Kenya as deadly ethnic clashes intensify in southern Ethiopia.

In another development, members of the first Refugee Youth Olympic Team, who fled conflict and violence, are now pursuing Olympic aspirations at the Dakar 2026 Games.
summary: A Nigerian court disqualified a leading presidential candidate, adding fresh complications to the electoral process two months before the election. Tens of thousands have fled across the border into Kenya as deadly ethnic clashes in southern Ethiopia intensify, and members of the first Refugee Youth Olympic Team are chasing Olympic dreams at Dakar 2026.

content: The landslide victory of the Students' List in Serbia's general election seems to have removed a blockage in the justice system: Cases that were long stalled are now suddenly moving forward.
summary: The Students' List secured a landslide victory in Serbia's recent general election. After the win, long‑stalled cases are moving forward, prompting new arrests and investigations.

content: U.S. midterm election results indicated that Donald Trump’s Iran war is unpopular among American voters. Gulf nations, which have been caught in the conflict between the United States and Iran for several months, say the outcome gives them reason to be optimistic about a possible end to the fighting.
summary: The US midterm results showed that Donald Trump's Iran war is unpopular with American voters. Gulf countries, trapped for months in the war between the US and Iran, say they are optimistic about an end.

content: Two new Ebola vaccine candidates are being added to an ongoing clinical trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The expansion occurs while the DRC continues to confront a deadly outbreak driven by the Bundibugyo species of the virus.

content: Attacks that damaged or destroyed water and sanitation systems in conflict zones increased threefold from 2021 to 2025. The surge in these attacks has heightened children’s exposure to disease outbreaks, malnutrition and violence.

content: The UN’s peacekeeping chief told the Security Council on Thursday that drone strikes in the disputed Abyei region killed at least 30 people last month. He said the attacks have added “a new and concerning dimension” to the area’s security situation.

content: UN Secretary‑General António Guterres said through his spokesperson on Thursday that he remains concerned about the situation on the Korean Peninsula, including the risk of an escalation of tensions across the Demilitarized Zone.

title: England cancer diagnoses top 1,000 daily, a record high
content: Cancer diagnoses in England have reached a record level, with NHS data showing that more than 1,000 people are diagnosed each day. Experts note that, despite the increase in case identification, the health service is not meeting its timescale targets for both diagnosis and treatment. They warn that the growing number of identified cases is not being matched by timely follow‑up, highlighting ongoing challenges in delivering prompt cancer care.
summary: Cancer diagnoses in England have reached a record high of more than 1,000 people per day, according to NHS figures. Experts say the NHS is still missing its timescale targets for diagnosis and treatment despite identifying more cases.

title: Metropolitan Police investigate two additional rape allegations against Russell Brand
content:
Police are investigating two additional rape allegations against comedian Russell Brand. The Metropolitan Police’s strategic lead, Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy, said the investigation remains ongoing and urged any other potential victims to come forward.  

Brand, 51, also faces a civil claim in the United Kingdom. Furphy described him as “a predator” whose behaviour, according to the detective, escalated as his fame grew.
summary: The Metropolitan Police, led by Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy, are investigating two further rape allegations against comedian Russell Brand, who is 51.

title: British doctor with Ebola evacuated from DR Congo arrives at Royal Free Hospital
content:
A British doctor who tested positive for Ebola while working in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has been returned to the United Kingdom for specialist care. The Department of Health and Social Care said the patient, whose identity has not been disclosed, was flown home on a medical evacuation flight on Thursday.

The doctor is now being treated in the high‑level isolation unit at the Royal Free Hospital in Hampstead, north London, which provides specialised care for infectious diseases.
summary: British doctor with Ebola evacuated from DR Congo arrives at Royal Free Hospital.
author: Guardian World

title: Yemen's president sacks ministers and officers to reverse war setbacks
content:
Yemen’s president has dismissed several ministers and senior officers, a move linked to recent Houthi gains and calls from southern Yemenis for greater influence. The UN‑recognised government reshuffled its political and military leadership to try to recapture territory lost to the Houthis in September and to end a four‑week siege of Taiz, the nation’s third‑largest city.

The effort follows a counter‑offensive launched on 5 October that sought to free the country from Houthi control but has stalled, leaving thousands dead on both sides. Despite Saudi Arabia’s air superiority and its need to repel near‑daily Houthi attacks on its own airports and bases, ground progress remains limited.
summary: The UN‑recognised Yemeni government dismissed several ministers and military officers after Houthi victories and pressure from southern Yemenis. The reshuffle follows a failed 5 October counteroffensive that left thousands dead and has not lifted the four‑week siege of Taiz despite Saudi air support.
author: Guardian World

title: Hoax bomb threats disrupt at least 25 European flights on Thursday
content:
Hoax bomb threats have disrupted at least 25 flights across Europe, forcing some aircraft to make emergency landings. The alerts, issued two days after a wave of false bomb warnings, have raised questions about a possible coordinated effort to create chaos for travellers.

The series of warnings on Thursday affected flights between Italy, Ireland, the United Kingdom, Spain, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Finland, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Portugal, France, Greece, Serbia, and Czechia. Each of these routes experienced diversions or emergency landings as airlines responded to the safety alerts.
summary: Hoax bomb threats caused disruption to at least 25 flights across Europe, with some planes forced to make emergency landings or diversions. The warnings on Thursday affected flights between Italy, Ireland, the UK, Spain, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Finland, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Portugal, France, Greece, Serbia and Czechia.
author: Guardian World

content: Philippine official says there are ‘signs that point to Thomas Markle Jr’s involvement in crime’, but he’s not yet being treated as a suspect The Duchess of Sussex’s estranged half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, has been named as a “person of interest” in the Philippine authorities’ inquiry into child sexual abuse image allegations made against her father, Thomas Markle Sr. The country’s interior and local government secretary, Jonvic Remulla, told a press conference in Manila there were “signs that point that the son is involved in the crime as well”.

title: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigns as Ueno Bank crisis freezes millions' savings
content:
Paraguay’s right‑wing president, Santiago Peña, resigned on Thursday following a political and financial crisis that collapsed the country’s banking system. The resignation came after millions of people’s savings were frozen amid the turmoil.

The crisis centers on Ueno Bank, which Peña’s administration had authorised to expand operations dramatically. Under his tenure the digital‑only bank grew from an obscure startup to one of Paraguay’s largest lenders, claiming roughly 60 % of the adult population as customers before its collapse.
summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigns as Ueno Bank crisis freezes millions' savings.

title: Early Black Friday beginner telescope deal — this portable Celestron is now 25% off at Amazon
content:
An early Black Friday deal is currently available for the Celestron Travel Scope 70, a portable telescope designed for beginners. The device is priced at $90 on Amazon, representing a $30 discount from its standard cost. This offer is part of a broader selection of early deals ahead of Black Friday, which is scheduled for November 27. The telescope is marketed as an entry-level option suitable for children and those testing their interest in astronomy before investing in more expensive equipment.

The Celestron Travel Scope 70 features a 70mm aperture with fully coated optics, providing views of the moon, planets, and some deep-sky objects. It includes a collapsible, full-height tripod, a carry bag, a finderscope, and Celestron’s Starry Night Software Basic Edition. The package also contains two eyepieces: one 10mm and one 20mm. These components are intended to give new users a functional starting point for observing celestial bodies without requiring significant storage space or a large financial commitment.

Reviewers have noted that the telescope is particularly ideal for beginner astronomers and children. A review of the Celestron Moon Mission Travel Scope 70, which is described as the same telescope with a lunar-themed skin, awarded it three and a half stars. The reviewer, Gemma Lavender, was impressed by the moon views delivered by the instrument. The review consensus on Amazon praises the model’s ease of assembly and portability, highlighting its suitability for those who want a lightweight option that can be taken on trips.

While the telescope does not offer the highest definition views, it is considered adequate for observing the moon, Jupiter, and some star clusters. It serves as a budget-friendly alternative to larger models that may require dedicated floor space or observatories. The current price of $90 is consistent with listings at B&H Photo and Best Buy. However, this is the lowest price the scope has reached since Amazon’s June Prime Day event, when it was available for $81.

The article recommends the Celestron Travel Scope 70 for total beginners or those needing a lightweight, portable option. It suggests that individuals seeking a telescope with more room to grow as their experience increases may want to look at more expensive models. The source notes that while many higher-end telescopes offer greater expandability, the Travel Scope 70 provides a low-risk entry into specialized optics for those just starting their skywatching journey.
summary: Black Friday is still weeks away but we've spotted this early telescope deal on a Celestron telescope designed with beginners in mind. The Celestron Travel Scope 70 is a great entry-level telescope that delivers better views of the moon, planets and some deep-sky objects.
author: Space.com

title: Voyager 1 Resolves 48-Hour Communications Glitch in Interstellar Space
content:
NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s most distant spacecraft, has re-established contact with Earth after a brief communications interruption. The probe stopped transmitting for approximately 48 hours between October 18 and 20 due a glitch that the spacecraft resolved autonomously before engineers could implement a remote fix. Kareem Badaruddin, the Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), noted in an agency statement that this was the first time the spacecraft had handled such an event independently, though the team expects unexpected issues at this stage of the mission.

Investigators determined that the communication loss occurred when one group of thrusters went offline, triggering the automatic activation of backup thrusters. This swap is programmed to occur if the spacecraft’s computers detect issues with the active thrusters, effectively placing the vehicle into a safe mode. Although engineers are still investigating the specific cause of the initial loss, the signal reappeared on October 20, and the Deep Space Network has since resumed its regular check-ins.

The incident highlights the challenges of managing a spacecraft located almost one light-day from Earth. At this distance, commands take nearly a day to reach the probe, and responses take another day to return. Voyager 1 is scheduled to reach the exact one-light-day milestone on November 18, at a distance of 16.09 billion miles (25.89 billion kilometers) from Earth.

Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, launched in 1977 to explore the outer solar system. Voyager 1 altered its trajectory after visiting Jupiter and Saturn, placing it high above the solar system’s plane, while Voyager 2 continued to Uranus and Neptune. Both spacecraft have since crossed into interstellar space and remain operational, powered by nuclear sources that are currently diminishing.

To address the declining power supply, engineers recently executed a power adjustment nicknamed the “Big Bang” in early September. This process involved turning off three devices on Voyager 1 and substituting them with lower-power alternatives, a similar adjustment made to Voyager 2 approximately six weeks prior. Each spacecraft loses four watts of power annually from an initial 470 watts, but these reconfigurations allow the missions to continue operating science instruments longer than previously anticipated. Suzanne Dodd, the project manager for Voyager at JPL, stated in 2022 that the mission is hoped to continue operating into the 2030s.
summary: NASA's Voyager 1 probe autonomously recovered from a 48-hour communications loss caused by a thruster swap into safe mode. Engineers are still investigating the incident, which occurred as the spacecraft approaches a distance of one light-day from Earth.
author: Space.com

title: Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover says human connection matters more than space views
content: TENERIFE, Canary Islands — Imagine traveling over 250 million miles from home, watching Earth disappear behind the moon and losing contact with the billions of people who call it home. What would you miss most? For Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover, the answer wasn't a particular place, a familiar view or even the comforts of home. It was something much more fundamental: human connection. Speaking during a discussion with former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival on Oct. 18 in Tenerife, Canary Islands, Glover reflected on the extraordinary experience of traveling around the moon and how being so far from Earth had given him a renewed appreciation for the people living on it. "The greatest reason to go to space, it isn't to be a swashbuckler hero," Glover said. "It's to do something that only 651 people have been able to do: miss Earth and miss other Earthlings." Glover was one of the four astronauts aboard NASA's Artemis II mission, which launched on April 1, 2026, marking humanity's first crewed journey to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. Alongside NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, the crew traveled farther from Earth than any humans before them. As the Orion spacecraft traversed the far side of the moon, the Artemis II crew watched Earth disappear below the lunar horizon before losing radio contact with our planet. Around 40 minutes later, Earth came back into view as the spacecraft emerged from behind the moon. NASA’s Orion spacecraft captures the Moon and the Earth in one frame during the Artemis II crew’s deep space journey at 6:39 p. M. ET on the sixth day of the mission. (Image credit: NASA) For Glover, however, the experience was about much more than the view. He believes that if everyone on Earth had the opportunity to make the same journey, they would come away with a similar appreciation for what they'd left behind. "I think all of us would say something in our native language, in the most basic way we can communicate about love, joy, hope and inspiration," Glover said. Although Glover shared the extraordinary journey with three fellow astronauts, the four of them were separated from the rest of humanity by hundreds of thousands of miles. And for Glover, that distance brought with it a strange contradiction: the farther he traveled from humanity, the more he longed to connect with it. "At the point of ultimate disconnection, [there is] this longing for connection," Glover said. The experience gave him a perspective that he carried back into everyday life. "There are moments where I am rushing through traffic and want to get where I'm going because I'm being selfish," Glover admitted. "But I don't have to stay there." Instead, he remembers what it felt like to look back at a planet so distant that everyone who has ever lived could be covered by his hand. "I wish you could all feel what it's like to come back home after that disconnection," he said. Victor Glover speaking at Starmus VIII, explaining how it felt to experience complete disconnection from everyone on Earth during Artemis II. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic/Future) The 'sea level effect' Astronauts often describe experiencing the "overview effect", a profound shift in perspective that can come from seeing Earth from space. But Glover believes that there's something equally powerful waiting to be discovered much closer to home. When asked by a Starmus VIII attendee whether people needed to undergo something extraordinary to develop a greater sense of kindness toward others, his answer was no. Glover encouraged people to look more closely at the natural world around them, whether that meant walking along the beach, watching the ocean or simply examining a leaf held up to sunlight. Even something as ordinary as a leaf, he explained, is capable of turning sunlight into food through photosynthesis. And although science can explain how that happens, understanding the process doesn't make it any less remarkable. "We have to choose to be moved by these things," Glover said. He worries that modern life, with its endless technological distractions, has made it all too easy to overlook the extraordinary things happening around us. "Familiarity breeds contempt. Have you heard this? I think it's worse than that. Familiarity breeds indifference," he said. Glover's "sea-level effect" encourages us all to rediscover the wonder of the natural world, right here on Earth. (Image credit: FanPro via Getty Images) Glover has a name for this perspective he hopes people can rediscover without traveling into space: The sea level effect. It's about finding the same sense of wonder and connection that astronauts experience in orbit, but right here on Earth, where most of us spend our lives. And ultimately, Glover believes the greatest wonder isn't the moon, the stars, or even the incredible complexity of nature. It's the people we share our planet with. "I think the hardest place to see this miracle is in the actual greatest miracle in the universe: other humans," he said. "We all feel it with babies, but when we get old enough to have opinions, we start to want to argue with each other." Glover hopes that by taking the time to appreciate the natural world, people might become a little more willing to appreciate one another too. "That's the mission that I want to be part of for the rest of my life," Glover said.
summary: During a discussion at the Starmus VIII festival, Victor Glover stated that his journey around the moon highlighted the value of human connection over physical surroundings. He encouraged the public to find this same sense of wonder in the natural world on Earth rather than requiring a spaceflight to appreciate their planet.
author: Space.com

title: KJ Apa stars in new James Stewart biopic Jimmy
content:
The biopic Jimmy, starring KJ Apa, has been critiqued as a straightforward and simple-minded portrayal of actor James Stewart’s life. The film focuses specifically on Stewart’s willingness to serve in the military during World War II and the immediate period following the conflict. While the production is described as a missed opportunity due to its corny nature, Apa’s performance is noted as surprisingly solid.

The review contrasts Apa’s current role with his previous work as Archie Andrews on the television series Riverdale. In that role, the New Zealand actor often ceded scenes to dynamic co-stars such as Luke Perry, Camila Mendes, and Madelaine Petsch. In Jimmy, Apa faces the challenge of portraying a beloved icon with a distinctive Pennsylvania accent and a reputation for decency. The primary competitive threat to his performance is not from his co-stars, but from the audience’s existing memories of Stewart’s extensive filmography.

Despite the film's overall shortcomings, Apa delivers a reasonable imitation of Stewart’s distinctive voice and gangly physicality. The review highlights that while many can approximate Stewart’s clipped and urbane speaking style, Apa successfully captures the actor’s mannerisms, particularly in scenes of distress. He effectively portrays the way Stewart appeared to be on the verge of toppling over with overflowing emotion during intense moments. Although the recreation is not note-perfect or particularly surprising, the review concludes that Apa successfully disappears into the role.
summary: The film Jimmy focuses on James Stewart's military service during World War II and its immediate aftermath. The review describes the biopic as a straightforward and missed opportunity, despite noting that KJ Apa delivers a surprisingly solid performance.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Pixies bassist Emma Richardson opens painting show Hotwire My Heart
content:
Emma Richardson, the bassist and vocalist who joined the Pixies in 2024, is currently exhibiting her painting in a show titled Hotwire My Heart. Richardson, who previously played in the garage-rock trio Band of Skulls, creates large-scale canvases using vivid oils that explore themes of hedonism, desire, and the breadth of human experience. Her artistic practice is influenced by her musical background, particularly her interest in the transcendent.

Richardson enjoys observing viewers’ reactions to her work, noting that the paintings often function like Rorschach inkblot tests. She describes the visual ambiguity of her pieces, which can be interpreted as anything from a nebula or a god to an explosion, an implosion, or an orgasm. The exhibition provides a space for audiences to engage with these complex, baroque images and form their own interpretations of the ecstatic and terrifying elements present in the art.
summary: Emma Richardson, who joined the Pixies in 2024, has opened her painting exhibition titled Hotwire My Heart. The show features large oil canvases that explore themes of hedonism and human experience, drawing from her background as a musician.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Russell Brand: from Big Brother and Hollywood to convicted rapist
content:
Former comedian Russell Brand has been identified as a convicted rapist, marking a significant fall from his previous status in Hollywood and on the reality television program Big Brother. The article questions how Brand was permitted to act in plain sight for such an extended period, noting that he had long cultivated an extreme persona.

According to the source, Brand recounted a specific incident from the early 1990s during his time as a student at the Italia Conti theatre school. He described becoming fixated on a classmate, following her for 200 miles through London, and sneaking onto her train to Wigan without a ticket. Brand admitted that despite her clear lack of desire for his company, he proceeded to her family home and entered her bed. He characterized his actions as lying, dancing, and evoking the "spirit of Pan" until she removed her bra, before using tears and emotional blackmail to remove her underwear.
summary: The article describes how teenage Russell Brand followed a classmate for 200 miles to her family home in Wigan. It details his admission of using emotional blackmail to engage in sexual activity with the unwilling classmate.

title: First Black drag queen presidential candidate Joan Jett Blakk runs in 1992
content: In off-Broadway show Ms Blakk for President, Oscar-winning Moonlight writer Tarell Alvin McCraney explores a slice of under-appreciated queer history At the height of the Aids crisis, Chicago activist Terence Alan Smith put on his drag persona, Joan Jett Blakk, and announced she was running for president. Her slogan: “Lick Bush in ‘92!” Her platform: fire everyone in the White House and paint it pink, reroute the military budget towards education and healthcare, then give the land back to Indigenous people “and let them take it from there”. The campaign did not advance. But Blakk did make it on to the floor of the Democratic national convention by infiltrating Madison Square Garden (as Smith) and changing in the bathroom. The country saw its first Black drag queen presidential candidate.
summary: First Black drag queen presidential candidate Joan Jett Blakk runs in 1992.

title: Clara Serrajordi: Barcelona midfielder filling void left by Alexia Putellas
content:
Clara Serrajordi, an 18-year-old midfielder, is emerging as a key figure for Barcelona, described as filling the void left by Alexia Putellas. The article highlights her rapid integration into the first team under coach Pere Romeu, noting that she made her debut at age 17. Serrajordi has already made substantial contributions, including starting ahead of Aitana Bonmatí in the 2026 Champions League final.

The piece draws parallels between Serrajordi’s playing style and her hobby of chess, which she uses to disconnect from football. As a product of La Masia, she is characterized as always being one move ahead, with a strong awareness of the space around her and the importance of each teammate. The article frames her rise as a clear strategic move for the club, positioning her as a new central presence in the Blaugrana midfield.
summary: The 18-year-old made her first-team debut at 17 and started ahead of Aitana Bonmatí in the 2026 Champions League final. She is described as a La Masia-educated player who is filling the midfield void left by Alexia Putellas.

title: Wembanyama scores 52, grabs 24 as Spurs beat Mavericks 112-111
content:
Victor Wembanyama led the San Antonio Spurs to a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks, securing the team’s sixth consecutive win. The 22-year-old Frenchman recorded a career-best 52 points and 24 rebounds, along with eight blocks. Wembanyama secured the win by sinking the decisive free throw with 24.2 seconds remaining.

The Spurs home crowd responded with MVP chants for Wembanyama during the Wednesday game. His defensive performance included three blocks in a span of just 13 seconds in the second quarter, contributing to the team’s overall dominance in the matchup.
summary: Victor Wembanyama recorded a career-best 52 points and 24 rebounds while blocking eight shots to lead the San Antonio Spurs to a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks. The 22-year-old secured the win by sinking a decisive free throw with 24.2 seconds remaining, marking the team's sixth straight victory.

title: International break prompts Premier League managers to fear job insecurity
content:
The international break is approaching, marking a period where Premier League managers, including Michael Carrick, face scrutiny regarding their job security. The article notes that what was once a time for reset has become a time for rehire, with managers looking over their shoulders.

In a recent match against Roma, Manchester United secured a comeback victory. At the final whistle, the camera focused on Carrick shaking hands with Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini before appearing uncertain about the post-match protocol. The footage then showed director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada clapping with expressions described as ashen. The author compares their demeanor to fans applauding a deceased relative. The piece concludes by observing that football club personnel are often expected to maintain serious expressions, with players avoiding visible enjoyment after defeats and managers required to appear earnest, except during rare moments of unintentional humor such as a journalist’s phone ringing during a press conference.
summary: The article describes how the international break has become a period of anxiety for Premier League managers, who fear being dismissed. It highlights Manchester United manager Michael Carrick's uncertainty after a match and the tense atmosphere among club executives.

title: Tom Curry injury doubt for England vs Australia as twin Ben poised to start
content:
Tom Curry is a major doubt for England’s autumn opener against Australia on Sunday after sustaining an injury during Wednesday’s training session. The setback has disrupted Steve Borthwick’s back-row plans, with his twin brother Ben currently leading the race to start at openside flanker. Borthwick is set to finalize and announce the team selection on Friday afternoon.

Ben Curry, who has not played for England since 2025, is in pole position to wear the No7 jersey if his brother is unavailable. The injury occurred during a full-bore training session, posing a significant challenge for the head coach ahead of the crucial November campaign.
summary: Tom Curry is a major doubt for England's autumn opener against Australia after sustaining an injury during Wednesday's training session. His twin brother Ben is currently in pole position to start at openside flanker for the match.

title: Japan FA's Kozo Tashima to challenge Infantino for Fifa presidency
content:
Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association, has announced his intention to challenge Gianni Infantino in March’s Fifa presidential election. Tashima stated that he brings an “honest, sound, upright attitude” to the contest and is understood to have acted with the blessing of Uefa.

He is the second challenger to declare ahead of the 18 November deadline, following former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega. It remains unclear whether Vega has secured the backing of five of Fifa’s 211 member associations, a requirement to appear on the ballot in Rabat.
summary: Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association, has announced his intention to run against Gianni Infantino in March's Fifa presidential election. Tashima is the second challenger to declare ahead of the November 18 deadline, following former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega.
